String.Dest: Killing vampires is always a pleasure.

String.Dest: I'll take them down.

String.Dest: What do you think Rukar was doing here?

String.Dest: The source of the Blood has been destroyed.

String.Dest: You knew the truth about the Blood and Namira's plan, then?

String.Dest: What is your duty here?

String.Dest: What is Zenkali-Dra like?

String.Source: Comedy?
String.Dest: Comedy?

String.Source: Can you tell me one of your jokes?
String.Dest: Can you tell me one of your jokes?

String.Source: The giant voriplasm is dead.
String.Dest: The giant voriplasm is dead.

String.Source: And you haven't killed him yet?
String.Dest: And you haven't killed him yet?

String.Source: I have your assurance the Vampyrum Order won't betray me once this is done?
String.Dest: I have your assurance the Vampyrum Order won't betray me once this is done?

String.Source: Can you tell me anything else about your mistress?
String.Dest: Can you tell me anything else about your mistress?

String.Source: I killed the monsters and collapsed the tunnel.
String.Dest: I killed the monsters and collapsed the tunnel.

String.Source: I have the idol.
String.Dest: I have the idol.

String.Source: What is the Meat, though?
String.Dest: What is the Meat, though?

String.Source: What is Varladimath? Why is Viatrix interested in it?
String.Dest: What is Varladimath? Why is Viatrix interested in it?

String.Source: I thought the Hollow Princess was long dead.
String.Dest: I thought the Hollow Princess was long dead.

String.Source: I'll wipe them out. All of them.
String.Dest: I'll wipe them out. All of them.

String.Source: I'll drive them out.
String.Dest: I'll drive them out.

String.Source: Why are the Forsworn attacking the Old Lands?
String.Dest: Why are the Forsworn attacking the Old Lands?

String.Source: I'll be back soon with the samples.
String.Dest: I'll be back soon with the samples.

String.Source: Shouldn't take long. I'll do it.
String.Dest: Shouldn't take long. I'll do it.

String.Source: I'll slaughter them.
String.Dest: I'll slaughter them.

String.Source: I'll drive them back.
String.Dest: I'll drive them back.

String.Source: A noble task. I'd be honored.
String.Dest: A noble task. I'd be honored.

String.Source: I'd be happy to deliver the medicine.
String.Dest: I'd be happy to deliver the medicine.

String.Source: I'll recover what I can.
String.Dest: I'll recover what I can.

String.Dest: Will you be able to convince the others of the truth about the Old Blood?

String.Dest: Your note said you needed assistance?

String.Dest: I've destroyed the rotting roots.

String.Dest: I've rung the first three bells.

String.Source: The Church has taken enough from you. Give them what you can spare, but no more.
String.Dest: The Church has taken enough from you. Give them what you can spare, but no more.

String.Source: Many cultures view the Daedric Prince Namira as an avatar of the Void itself. To the Khajiit, she is Ur-Dra, the Great Darkness that exists beyond reality. To the Reachfolk, she is the queen of the spirits, who granted Lorkhan a place within the Void to create the world. Devout followers of Namira are sometimes transformed into embodiments of the Void themselves.
String.Dest: Many cultures view the Daedric Prince Namira as an avatar of the Void itself. To the Khajiit, she is Ur-Dra, the Great Darkness that exists beyond reality. To the Reachfolk, she is the queen of the spirits, who granted Lorkhan a place within the Void to create the world. Devout followers of Namira are sometimes transformed into embodiments of the Void themselves.

String.Source: Why struggle? Abandon yourself to Her Light.
String.Dest: Why struggle? Abandon yourself to Her Light.

String.Source: The drowned are not truly undead, for the corpses do not move on their own. Scholars call them by a more accurate term: "Voriplasmic Corpse," because the corpse is nothing but the puppet of the voriplasm.
String.Dest: The drowned are not truly undead, for the corpses do not move on their own. Scholars call them by a more accurate term: "Voriplasmic Corpse," because the corpse is nothing but the puppet of the voriplasm.

String.Source: Village myth claims that the entire hyena population in the Old Lands is the result of a single Khajjit traveler, who made the poor choice of taking his entire pack of hyenas to the Old Lands with him.
String.Dest: Village myth claims that the entire hyena population in the Old Lands is the result of a single Khajjit traveler, who made the poor choice of taking his entire pack of hyenas to the Old Lands with him.

String.Source: The xanmeers, also known as "stone nests," were build by ancient Argonians in an effort to resist the natural decay of the world. The ancient civilization collapsed in an event known as Duskfall, leaving the xanmeers abandoned.
String.Dest: The xanmeers, also known as "stone nests," were build by ancient Argonians in an effort to resist the natural decay of the world. The ancient civilization collapsed in an event known as Duskfall, leaving the xanmeers abandoned.

String.Source: The Dark Heart was an artifact of Namira that once rested in the caverns below Skyrim. An embodiment of pure Void, the Dark Heart nearly absorbed the souls of everyone in Skyrim during the Gray Host incident in the Second Era.
String.Dest: The Dark Heart was an artifact of Namira that once rested in the caverns below Skyrim. An embodiment of pure Void, the Dark Heart nearly absorbed the souls of everyone in Skyrim during the Gray Host incident in the Second Era.

String.Source: Nothing you do will matter. All shall glimmer below the Coldlight.
String.Dest: Nothing you do will matter. All shall glimmer below the Coldlight.

String.Source: "Among the foulest of these spirits is Kalarix Brood, the Writhing Mother. Worshippers of Kalarix Brood are generally unwilling, as any unfortunate afflicted with parasites is a servant of the Brood." - Greater Children of the Void
String.Dest: "Among the foulest of these spirits is Kalarix Brood, the Writhing Mother. Worshippers of Kalarix Brood are generally unwilling, as any unfortunate afflicted with parasites is a servant of the Brood." - Greater Children of the Void

String.Source: "Behold, the coldlight star!"
String.Dest: "Behold, the coldlight star!"

String.Source: Do you hear the hours?
String.Dest: Do you hear the hours?

String.Source: Some theorize that the xanmeers in the Old Lands are not individual structures, but rather the top parts of a single vast structure.
String.Dest: Some theorize that the xanmeers in the Old Lands are not individual structures, but rather the top parts of a single vast structure.

String.Source: Most Argonains have an instinctive fear of the xanmeers, viewing them as cursed remnants of a past best forgotten.
String.Dest: Most Argonains have an instinctive fear of the xanmeers, viewing them as cursed remnants of a past best forgotten.

String.Source: None can say what strange power animates the corpses within the xanmeers. Seeking such knowledge is a death sentence in itself.
String.Dest: None can say what strange power animates the corpses within the xanmeers. Seeking such knowledge is a death sentence in itself.

String.Source: There is no escaping the light of glass.
String.Dest: There is no escaping the light of glass.

String.Source: All is futile. Let the loving cold of the Glass Star end your sorrows.
String.Dest: All is futile. Let the loving cold of the Glass Star end your sorrows.

String.Source: The Forsworn desire the Old Blood as well. Not as a blessing, but a weapon to overthrow the Nords.
String.Dest: The Forsworn desire the Old Blood as well. Not as a blessing, but a weapon to overthrow the Nords.

String.Source: The Old Lands are sometimes attacked by the Forsworn, who seek to use the Old Blood for their dark rituals.
String.Dest: The Old Lands are sometimes attacked by the Forsworn, who seek to use the Old Blood for their dark rituals.

String.Source: Void Gems are clusters of crystalized Void energy. While pretty, the magic stored within any individual gem is too weak to be useful for anything but the most niche magic.
String.Dest: Void Gems are clusters of crystalized Void energy. While pretty, the magic stored within any individual gem is too weak to be useful for anything but the most niche magic.

String.Source: In the Second Era, a vampiric army known as the Gray Host attempted to steal the souls of all mortals in the Reach using magical storms known as Harrowstorms. Those caught within the storms were transformed into monstrous Harrowfiends, and their souls were fed to the Dark Heart, a Daedric relic of Namira.
String.Dest: In the Second Era, a vampiric army known as the Gray Host attempted to steal the souls of all mortals in the Reach using magical storms known as Harrowstorms. Those caught within the storms were transformed into monstrous Harrowfiends, and their souls were fed to the Dark Heart, a Daedric relic of Namira.

String.Source: Bloodcrabs are not originally native to the Old Lands. Rather, they were introduced to the Old Lands by immigrants from Tamriel who brought pet Mudcrabs with them. Over time, feeding on the native Bloodroots mutated these crabs into their current form.
String.Dest: Bloodcrabs are not originally native to the Old Lands. Rather, they were introduced to the Old Lands by immigrants from Tamriel who brought pet Mudcrabs with them. Over time, feeding on the native Bloodroots mutated these crabs into their current form.

String.Source: The Forsworn do not take kindly to Reachfolk who reject their cause. Clans that refuse to fight the Nords are the enemies of the Forsworn.
String.Dest: The Forsworn do not take kindly to Reachfolk who reject their cause. Clans that refuse to fight the Nords are the enemies of the Forsworn.

String.Source: Legends in Black Marsh tell of massive Voriplasms with the ability to speak and use magic. Most hope that those are only legends.
String.Dest: Legends in Black Marsh tell of massive Voriplasms with the ability to speak and use magic. Most hope that those are only legends.

String.Source: Voriplasms are a strange form of carnivorous slime native to Black Marsh. Unwary explorers are often devoured whole.
String.Dest: Voriplasms are a strange form of carnivorous slime native to Black Marsh. Unwary explorers are often devoured whole.

Azurah: The Great Lie by Rundah-dro, Speaker for the Blood

[pagebreak] Khajiit children are told to fear their hearts, for their hearts beat in time with Namiira. They are told to shut their ears, for, if they move to the Bent Dance, they will be lost. Their nightmares are filled with the screams of the dro-m'Athra. Khajiit children are told to love Azurah. They are told she protects them, keeps them safe from Namiira and Lorkhaj. That Her love is all that protects them from the Bent Cats. Khajiit children are told lies. [pagebreak] Azurah, the greedy. Azurah, the selfish. Azurah, the traitor. But the truth will not be buried. In the darkest reaches of the desert, a Root grew from the sands. I tore into the Root and drank of the Blood of the world, and, in the Blood, I knew the truth. The Root is the Blood. The Blood is the Root. The Heart of Lorkhaj is but one of a pair. The Dark Heart beats still, and it is the heartbeat of the Khajiit. I heard my heart, and thus I heard the truth. In the Great Darkness, all of Fadomai's Children had left Her. All save Lorkhaj. Lorkhaj stayed by Her side. Lorkhaj guarded Her. And, in the Great Darkness, Lorkhaj saw the truth. [pagebreak] The Darkness is not our foe. The Darkness is all that exists. The world within the Lunar Lattice is a lie, a prison constructed by Azurah. It keeps the cats from seeing their true selves. In the Darkness, Lorkhaj saw Himself. And, in Lorkhaj, the Darkness saw Itself. Their Hearts mingled, and thus was born Namiira, true mother of the Khajiit. Namiira carries the will of Fadomai, the truth of the Darkness. Namiira seeks to show us our true selves. Do not fear the Dark Heart. Do not fear the Bent Dance. Dance, fellow cats! Dance on the moonless nights, and embrace your true forms! Dance, dance, dance! Let your shackles fall away! [pagebreak] UR DRA NA MII RA UR DRA NA MII RA UR DRA NA MII RA!
String.Dest:
[pagebreak]

String.Source:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'> Mistress Caerellia, I am pleased to report that the so-called "Old Blood Cult" of Voidsucker vampires will pose no threat to our ambitions here in Skyrim.
The members of this cult, rather than drinking the blood of mortals, seek to emulate the ancient Nighthollow clan by drinking what they call "The Old Blood," a substance which flows below the ground of their mountain lair. The members of the cult believe this blood grants them incredible powers and, as such, drink it exclusively.
As my mission was to determine which of Skyrim's clans may interfere with your schemes, I infiltrated the cult and obtained a sample of their sacred "Old Blood," which I have now completed my study of. Alchemical analysis is clear: this "Blood" is in fact nothing more than modified Hist Sap.
While I am unsure of the exact composition of added ingredients, I can confidently state that the effects of this sap would be quite simple: it functions as a weaker, highly diluted blood potion, but with the unpleasant side effect of being exceptionally addictive, on the same level as an especially potent variety of Skooma.
In short, the vampires of the Voidsucker clan are nothing but mind-addled addicts, relying on a weak, addictive substitute for blood. This addiction also prevents them from venturing far from their home, as the "Old Blood" cannot be found anywhere else and decays quickly after extraction. This clan neither poses a threat nor presents any potential value to us and, as such, can be ignored entirely. </font>
String.Dest:

String.Source:
<font face='$SkyrimBooks' size='18'> While all who came to the Palace shared the worship of the Old Blood, it soon became apparent that their beliefs about the Blood differed. To the followers of the Hollow Princess, the Blood was merely a medium - a way to commune with the Void. They saw this realm as an interim one, through which they would ascend to be one with the true Darkness.
When the Princess realized not all shared her view, she cast them out of the palace, away from the source of the Blood.
"We are not heartless," said the Princess, "and so we will not deprive you of Blood. But the source shall be under our guard to prevent misuse." The others lacked the power to oppose the Princess, and so they agreed.
"Should the need arise - should the Blood be threatened - we will grant you a method of return." So saying, the Princess raised her arms, and Blood spewed forth from the ground. At her command, her attendants came, collecting the Blood in great urns.
"Take these to your new homes." She commanded. "Draw forth the iron within and forge them into grand bells, one for each of our clans."
Thus, the pact was forged, and the five bells cast. One in the forest on the borders of the founder's land. One to the southeast to watch the dance of the False Moon. One to the south to guard the Bloodsong tribe. One to the southwest, to swim with the Twisted Roots. And one vanished into shadows, secreted away by the Iceblood Clan.
Each clan would worship the Blood as they saw fit, and none would interfere with another. But should the day ever come when the clans face a mutual threat, the bells will herald the opening of the gates. </font>

The Hunter and the Bleeding Tree Part of the oral tradition of the Reach, compiled by Rallis Laurinum

[pagebreak] The legend of The Hunter and the Bleeding Tree predates even the oldest clans of The Reach, with one of the oldest recorded mentions dating back to circa 1E 1020, before even the Legend of Red Eagle. From my research, it seems that the tale, despite its several variations, will always begin with the errant arrow of a hunter: As the legend goes, a weary hunter of the Reach was tracking a wounded elk deep in the heart of the woods. He had been tracking the elk all day, and hunger and fatigue were wearing his bow arm down. As he drew his arrow upon the elk, his stomach erupted in a deep growl which startled the elk, causing it to leap from its resting place, bellowing as it did. The hunter, with a start, loosed the arrow, which sailed between its antlers and buried itself deep within the wood of an ancient, gnarled maple tree. [pagebreak] Cursing his luck, the poor hunter went to retrieve his arrow from the tree. Yet, upon reaching the tree, the hunter was met with a peculiar sight. His arrow, honed to a razor-sharp point, had embedded itself deep into the bark of the twisted maple. Seeping from the wound of the tree, a fresh stream of bright liquid now flowed as red as a ruby but dull as iron. At first, the hunter believed it to be sweet syrup, but, when he dared to have a taste, he was met with the metallic tang of blood. This tree, before his eyes, was bleeding bright, crimson blood. Intrigued, the hunter drew his knife and stabbed the tree. Once. Twice. Three times. Each time his blade pierced the warm bark, fresh blood spilled from the wounds he inflicted. [pagebreak] As he stabbed into the tree, it groaned. Whether this was just the wind through its boughs or some spirit within the tree, the groan seeded guilt deep within the hunter's heart. It was a wounded animal, and his duty as a hunter meant he must finish his kill lest Hircine himself send punishment. In each rendition of this legend, the poor hunter continues to stab and slice until its wounds are more numerous than the stars in the sky. The earth beneath his feet grew sodden with blood till it pooled at his ankles and soaked his clothes. Convinced this tree was the work of the daedra, the hunter fled, leaving his knife embedded in the tree. He had to return to his clan. He had to share his discovery. He had to consult the elders for fear he had gone mad. [pagebreak] The following morning, the hunter and his clan returned to the glade where the tree stood, yet no tree stood in the glade. Merely a dark, dried puddle of blood remained in its place, seemingly devouring the sunlight that bled through the canopy. The hunter swore upon his ancestors that there was a tree there yesterday, that the hole in the canopy used to contain the tree's crown, and that he left his knife in its bark, but his pleas fell on his unconvinced kin. They mocked him all the way back to their camp. Yet, each member, quietly to themselves, could not work out what creature could have left behind such a quantity of blood and left no carcass. There were no signs of a fight, no tracks, no depression or bones, and no knife. Just blood. [pagebreak] The clan and even the hunter soon forgot this devilish tree, and it became simply a tale around the campfire - much as it is now - until exactly one year had passed. One morning, the hunter was found in his tent after he had failed to rise for breakfast, his lost knife deep within his chest. Wounds coated his body, his cot soaked with his own blood. Yet the clan found no signs of a fight, no tracks, no sightings of anyone entering or leaving his tent. The hunter's tent was ordered to be burned, along with his body and belongings inside, and, even before the ashes lay cold, the clan had fled the area. To this day, on nights when the moon is but an empty disk, you can hear the sounds of the hunter's knife spilling the blood of the bleeding tree.

Greater Children of the Void

[pagebreak]

A note from the editor: This book is published in its original, unfinished state. When our representatives visited the author to collect the completed product, they discovered that he had apparently suffocated due to being force-fed his own eyes. We choose to believe that the incident is unrelated to the contents of this book. However, out of an abundance of caution - and because, despite our best efforts, we could not locate even a single scholar who could corroborate any of the claims made herein - we would like to emphasize that we are publishing this as a work of fiction. [pagebreak] While the daedra and their Princes are well-known to the public of Tamriel, far fewer are aware of those entities who dwell within the Void beyond Aurbis. This is only natural, as even passing between the Void and Oblivion is a difficult task, and few of the entities within the Void have any interest in (or awareness of) the Aurbis - something for which we should be thankful, as should some of the truly grand Void Spirits take note of our reality, even Oblivion and Aetherius would likely cease to be. [pagebreak] Of the spirits that have crossed from the Void into the Aurbis, most are considered lesser spirits, such as the Shades and Voidmothers that follow Namira. Indeed, of the greater Void Spirits, Namira herself is likely the only one known to most of Mundus. However, there do exist several other greater spirits who have managed to manifest in the Aurbis, albeit not in their full power. These spirits instead have bypassed the Sacred Numbers protecting the Aurbic wheel and entered Oblivion through weakened avatars, roughly equivalent to the various Daedric Lords and Demiprinces already known to exist throughout Oblivion. To better illuminate these mysterious spirits, I have chosen to document thirteen [four. -Editor] of the ones I find most interesting. [pagebreak]

Millamaste, the Golden

Of the spirits who have crossed over from the Void, Millamaste is one of the more active in worldly affairs, with several small cults dedicated to her throughout Tamriel. Worship of Millamaste is often confused with that of Sheogorath (and indeed, Millamaste has frequently been observed following the bidding of the Prince of Madness) or Sanguine due to an emphasis on madness, alcohol, art, and misuse of the Dibellic arts. In reality, however, Millamaste's sphere is none of these - rather, she embodies the concept of "loss of control." When one gives in to their instincts, be they for violence, music, or drink, Millamaste is pleased. Her realm, the Spiral City, is a demiplane of Oblivion that once belonged to the Shivering Isles before being gifted to her by Sheogorath, who had grown bored with it. The residents of the Spiral City work endlessly to expand the city, but due to their madness, along with an enchantment on the realm preventing them from communicating or even perceiving one another, the City has become an endless maze with no possible method of navigation, designed to increase the madness of its populace. In artistic representations, Millamaste is depicted as a four-armed woman with golden skin and long insect legs taking the place of hair. [pagebreak]

Kalarix Brood, the Writhing Mother

Among the foulest of these spirits is Kalarix Brood, patron of insects. A close ally (or servant) of Namira, Kalarix considers all creatures that dwell within rot to be her children and especially favors parasites (interestingly, despite the myriad diseases caused by parasites, Kalarix has no known connection to Peyrite). Worshippers of Kalarix Brood are generally unwilling, as any unfortunate afflicted with parasites is a servant of the Brood. Her realm, the Writhing Hive, is a demiplane connected to the Scuttling Void. The realm is said to be made entirely of living insects, primarily parasites, endlessly crawling over one another in an orgy of rot. In statues, Kalarix Brood is generally depicted as a tall figure made entirely of insects combined into a roughly bipedal shape. However, in some rare depictions, Kalarix is instead shown as an Elven child. The reason for this discrepancy is unknown. [pagebreak]

Anananis, the Weaver

The most unusual of the spirits, little is known about Anananis. She has no worshippers on Mundus and seems entirely uninterested in the affairs of the world, only answering a summoning once in all of recorded history. In this instance, a group of Psijjic mages inquired to her as to her sphere of influence, to which she replied, "I/We weave/wove/will weave the Dream." The changes in tense and pronoun, as depicted here, are my best attempt at representing how Anananis spoke, as she apparently said all variants simultaneously. This answer was seemingly satisfactory to the Psijjic Order, as the only other record left of the summoning was that her actions "are not a concern to Mundus." Anananis has no known plane of Oblivion nor any known ties to other daedra. Some rare depictions seem to show her as a spider daedra, but this is believed to be artistic liberty and does not denote an association with Mephala. Likewise, it should be noted that her comments regarding "the Dream" are not to be taken as a literal reference to dreams - in other words, to Vaermina's sphere of influence - but rather to the Dreamsleeve, an unrelated concept which [Editor's note: We were unable to locate the next five pages. The next page we were able to locate appears to be the conclusion of another section.] As such, Tohvi Kajh is known to have provided his patronage to several clans in Black Marsh, but as no other records prior to the events of Duskfall can be found, his exact relationship to the Xanmeers is unknown. [pagebreak]
String.Dest:
[pagebreak]

Greater Children of the Void

[pagebreak]

A note from the editor: This book is published in its original, unfinished state. When our representatives visited the author to collect the completed product, they discovered that he had apparently suffocated due to being force-fed his own eyes. We choose to believe that the incident is unrelated to the contents of this book. However, out of an abundance of caution - and because, despite our best efforts, we could not locate even a single scholar who could corroborate any of the claims made herein - we would like to emphasize that we are publishing this as a work of fiction. [pagebreak] While the daedra and their Princes are well-known to the public of Tamriel, far fewer are aware of those entities who dwell within the Void beyond Aurbis. This is only natural, as even passing between the Void and Oblivion is a difficult task, and few of the entities within the Void have any interest in (or awareness of) the Aurbis - something for which we should be thankful, as should some of the truly grand Void Spirits take note of our reality, even Oblivion and Aetherius would likely cease to be. [pagebreak] Of the spirits that have crossed from the Void into the Aurbis, most are considered lesser spirits, such as the Shades and Voidmothers that follow Namira. Indeed, of the greater Void Spirits, Namira herself is likely the only one known to most of Mundus. However, there do exist several other greater spirits who have managed to manifest in the Aurbis, albeit not in their full power. These spirits instead have bypassed the Sacred Numbers protecting the Aurbic wheel and entered Oblivion through weakened avatars, roughly equivalent to the various Daedric Lords and Demiprinces already known to exist throughout Oblivion. To better illuminate these mysterious spirits, I have chosen to document thirteen [four. -Editor] of the ones I find most interesting. [pagebreak]

Millamaste, the Golden

Of the spirits who have crossed over from the Void, Millamaste is one of the more active in worldly affairs, with several small cults dedicated to her throughout Tamriel. Worship of Millamaste is often confused with that of Sheogorath (and indeed, Millamaste has frequently been observed following the bidding of the Prince of Madness) or Sanguine due to an emphasis on madness, alcohol, art, and misuse of the Dibellic arts. In reality, however, Millamaste's sphere is none of these - rather, she embodies the concept of "loss of control." When one gives in to their instincts, be they for violence, music, or drink, Millamaste is pleased. Her realm, the Spiral City, is a demiplane of Oblivion that once belonged to the Shivering Isles before being gifted to her by Sheogorath, who had grown bored with it. The residents of the Spiral City work endlessly to expand the city, but due to their madness, along with an enchantment on the realm preventing them from communicating or even perceiving one another, the City has become an endless maze with no possible method of navigation, designed to increase the madness of its populace. String.Source:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'> Some of you will shun me for the steps I have taken. Some of you will shun me merely for resorting to the written word to deliver my message. But some of you will see the potential.
The Old Blood is the primal magic from which Lorkh created this world. It is the primal blood of creation itself. And with it, we can bring an end to the Silver-Bloods. An end to ALL Nords. Those of you who have courage, who are willing to do what must be done: come to the ruins of the Eye of Markarth. We are stockpiling the Blood taken from the caravans there, and when the barrels are filled, we will use it to destroy the tyrants of Markarth.
- Vateshran Iorus </font>

String.Source:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'> Pardon the interruption - I'm sure your duties to the Cronvangr Clan are keeping you quite occupied, but I have information I believe may be of use to you. Have you heard of the Voidsucker Clan? Or perhaps their more common name, the "Old-Blood Vampires?"
One of my agents is currently present in the Old Lands and noted your presence. I imagine that, like myself, you've realized that the position of Skyrim's vampires would be jeopardized were the feral Voidsuckers and Drybloods to escape the Old Lands and begin attacking mortals in Skyrim proper. After all, the last thing any vampire wants is for the mortals to rally against them.
My agent is working to dismantle the Voidsuckers already, but if you consider this matter to be worth your attention, seek out my agent. His name is Capiton Esdrescus, and his last report suggested he had made a base of operations in the forest region of the Old Lands. Show him this note, and he will be obligated to assist. -VC

String.Source: Perhaps the issue is the human-like appearance selected for the Vessel. The more human the body, the more like a human the spirit that possesses it? Perhaps it's merely coincidental. Even so, I will modify the backup Vessel to be less human-like. I don't want something fully bestial - it must be capable of obeying my orders - but the addition of some animalistic traits may help. Perhaps a smaller body, as well - children are more obedient, are they not?

String.Source: The waiting is the most frustrating part. My aged body is too weak to infiltrate the Palace myself, and sending the Vessel unescorted risks its destruction. The sellswords I hire never survive long enough... I'm forced to sit and wait in the hopes someone stronger falls for the bait I've left. Duraeg appears to be growing suspicious of my activities. I may need to deal with him...

String.Source: <font face='$HandwrittenFont'> From what I've overheard, it seems there are multiple keys to the belltower. Each key is held by one of the leaders of the dro-m'Athra - the Rajaska. It seems each Rajaska controls one of the nearby ruins - Seribani Sallidadna, Zhanlaj Zhanzalv, and Aydithozay Zha'morna. One of them surely has the key I require. Now all I need to do is sneak back out of this cave...

String.Source:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'> No disrespect to Clanmother Svenja, who has kept our clan alive, but we cannot stay in only a single cave. Cronvangr Hall's location keeps it secure and well-hidden, but also makes it difficult to reach places where mortals congregate. If we are to thrive as a proper vampire clan, we will need outposts.
For our first outpost, I've selected the old caves by Shor's Stone, where the giant Sinmur was entombed after his defeat by Ysgramor. The locals have a superstitious fear of these caves, making them an ideal hiding spot. If anyone does investigate, the spectral guardians I've brought from Cronvangr Temple will deal with them.
</font>

String.Source:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'> These caverns go far deeper than I'd expected. Sinmur's tomb was but the surface - we've uncovered a vast network, seemingly carved by the same water that feeds the hot springs above. I suspect the fumes from the springs are the source of this delightful red mist, as well.
The locals have taken notice of our presence, but we have a prepared cover story - we are miners, seeking our fortune in the depths of Redbelly. The mortals warned us not to dig too deep lest we awaken Sinmur, but otherwise seemed unconcerned by our presence. In fact, I think I saw the gleam of greed in their eyes - if this becomes a productive mine, the village will become rich. That greed will prevent them from realizing our true identities until it's too late.
</font>

String.Source:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'> I had to scold Ylfra today. She's an eager lass with a strong affinity for the spiders, but she's a bit TOO fond of them. If she lets them breed too quickly, they'll overrun the cave and venture out into the village - and even if that doesn't alert the mortals to our identities, it will convince them that the mine is too dangerous. The Cronvangr vampires hunt secretly. We cannot risk exposure.
</font>

<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'> We've been surprisingly successful at mining. Many of the mortals have joined the mine in the hopes of striking iron - or, better yet, ebony - and their greed is such that they're willing to write off any disappearances as simply "mining accidents." As long as we ensure none of the corpses are found - and that nobody spots us feeding - we can keep this going for decades.
</font>

Until she arrives, I've asked our guards to ensure nobody approaches that vein.
</font>

<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'> My fellows are unhappy with the presence of an elf, but nobody knows more about alchemy than Morilye. I trust her to solve the mystery of this strange ore.
That said, I was surprised by how eager she was to come. The elves of Varladimath are incredibly reclusive, hated both by the Alessians and their own fellow Ayleids, but she was delighted by the invitation. She keeps muttering about "a chance to commune with the Princess," whatever that means. As long as she can analyze the ore, she's welcome to talk to the voices in her head as much as she likes.
</font>

<font face='$HandwrittenFont'> N, For all your bold talk about your mastery over the secrets of the Void, it seems I've once again come out ahead. While you labor in esoteric ritual, I have claimed the Dark Heart for myself. My Vessel - my new Numidium - will soon be ready, charged with the energies of the Void, and I will reshape the Aurbis to my whims.
Just as you always gloated to me about your successes in Cyrodiil, I shall do the same for you. Come to my workshop here in the Old Lands. There is a circle of standing stones in the forest - simply cast a Voidlight spell within the circle, and the chamber shall open. I look forward to greeting you in my new role as ruler of reality. -R </font>

String.Source:
[pagebreak]

On the Clans of the Reach: An Extended Study by Theopho Harvian, Imperial Scribe 2E 588

[pagebreak] It has been now twenty years since last I wrote of, or even saw, the Reach and its mighty spirit. My first volume detailed Tamriel's misconception of the Reachclans' unruliness, their ongoing anarchy, and just how much we had to learn of their true natures. An older and wiser scribe now, permit me to muse at just how deeply we have scrubbed and shined the mirror at ourselves in the interim: Cyrodiil without an Emperor since Clivia Tharn - herself a Reach descendent - and the Elder Council's waxing and waning of alliances to match even the bloodiest of Reach feuds. [pagebreak] Though my days of trade embassies have passed, I once more visited Markarth and toured the wider Druadach region with my apprentice. Some clans continue to thrive, whilst others have passed to obscurity like the rolling mists above the Karth - and more still are freshly formed, as fluid as I described in my prior study. It is a comfort to know that - in such change - nothing has changed at all. In that way, the Reach - for all its 'bloody' customs and proclivities - reflects a token of humanity most would take for granted. [pagebreak] At the time of this second excursion, the following clans are either the more prominent - or of most academic intrigue - to any fellow traveler to the Reach. Crow-Watcher Clan: Smaller in number than many of its neighboring clans, the Crow-Watchers are reclusive enough to provide little story of their own. Much like their namesake corvids, they appear to adopt a more surveillant role in lieu of any notable combative strength; living high in the Druadach Mountains and oft taking perch in trees, keeping watch for threats and feeding information to more powerful clans in exchange for "protection." [pagebreak] Cinder-Heart Clan: A warlike clan once settled near Markarth, but recently adopting a more nomadic lifestyle - such to "blaze might across all the Reach." Already infamous for their burning of captives alive, and gruesome method of crafting Briarhearts, their formidable claim to eminence across the region sees them now also brand their young with scorching chains: a mark of duty to the clan, their scars forever binding them to serve the searing hunt. [pagebreak] Eagleseer Clan: A large and proud clan, continuing only to grow. Following their bid for glory against the Grey Host six years past, it seems their hunger for Reach feuds has only strengthened: no doubt the taste of such honor propelling a new era of bloodlust. Amusingly, they are also notably more welcoming of outsiders than before - their now-grown children recognising my 'strange voice' and calling me "Good Freehand." Yet still we are not worthy of a feud! [pagebreak] Elk-Runner Clan: A small band of disparate Reachfolk passionately at odds with the River-Elk Clan, having formed from disillusioned or discarded members of said clan. The similarity in name is likely a ploy to divert foreign trade from the River-Elks; and the use of its domesticated elk stock in carting wares at a remarkable pace throughout the Karth Valley and beyond. [pagebreak] Wildspear Clan: Once a prominent clan, their hostility toward Reach-kin and outsiders alike has finally seen reply. Now all but four proud spears remain following a massacre by the Thornroot Clan; goaded into the hunt by its hags, owing to the Wildspear's steadfast honoring of Hircine with "clever prey." [pagebreak] Worm-Tender Clan: A small yet covetous pack of maggot worshippers. Residing only in quags or waterlogged caves, they venerate the filth and rot of Namira. Unlike the decorated pelts and vestments unique to most Reachfolk, the Worm-Tenders clothe themselves solely in the mud of their fetid swamps. All creatures, from worm to wolf, they devour whole to honor "Mother" -- such that hearing only absolute silence when walking the Reach means but one thing: you are the last meal left to be hunted.
String.Dest:
[pagebreak]

Some clans continue to thrive, whilst others have passed to obscurity like the rolling mists above the Karth - and more still are freshly formed, as fluid as I described in my prior study. It is a comfort to know that - in such change - nothing has changed at all. In that way, the Reach - for all its 'bloody' customs and proclivities - reflects a token of humanity most would take for granted. [pagebreak] At the time of this second excursion, the following clans are either the more prominent - or of most academic intrigue - to any fellow traveler to the Reach. Crow-Watcher Clan: Smaller in number than many of its neighboring clans, the Crow-Watchers are reclusive enough to provide little story of their own. Much like their namesake corvids, they appear to adopt a more surveillant role in lieu of any notable combative strength; living high in the Druadach Mountains and oft taking perch in trees, keeping watch for threats and feeding information to more powerful clans in exchange for "protection." [pagebreak] Cinder-Heart Clan: A warlike clan once settled near Markarth, but recently adopting a more nomadic lifestyle - such to "blaze might across all the Reach." Already infamous for their burning of captives alive, and gruesome method of crafting Briarhearts, their formidable claim to eminence across the region sees them now also brand their young with scorching chains: a mark of duty to the clan, their scars forever binding them to serve the searing hunt. [pagebreak] Eagleseer Clan: A large and proud clan, continuing only to grow. Following their bid for glory against the Grey Host six years past, it seems their hunger for Reach feuds has only strengthened: no doubt the taste of such honor propelling a new era of bloodlust. Amusingly, they are also notably more welcoming of outsiders than before - their now-grown children recognising my 'strange voice' and calling me "Good Freehand." Yet still we are not worthy of a feud! [pagebreak] Elk-Runner Clan: A small band of disparate Reachfolk passionately at odds with the River-Elk Clan, having formed from disillusioned or discarded members of said clan. The similarity in name is likely a ploy to divert foreign trade from the River-Elks; and the use of its domesticated elk stock in carting wares at a remarkable pace throughout the Karth Valley and beyond. [pagebreak] Wildspear Clan: Once a prominent clan, their hostility toward Reach-kin and outsiders alike has finally seen reply. Now all but four proud spears remain following a massacre by the Thornroot Clan; goaded into the hunt by its hags, owing to the Wildspear's steadfast honoring of Hircine with "clever prey." [pagebreak] Worm-Tender Clan: A small yet covetous pack of maggot worshippers. Residing only in quags or waterlogged caves, they venerate the filth and rot of Namira. Unlike the decorated pelts and vestments unique to most Reachfolk, the Worm-Tenders clothe themselves solely in the mud of their fetid swamps. All creatures, from worm to wolf, they devour whole to honor "Mother" -- such that hearing only absolute silence when walking the Reach means but one thing: you are the last meal left to be hunted.

String.Source:
[pagebreak]

Dro-m'Athra: Dancers of the Mind by Helaena Carolus

[pagebreak] It is a myth oft perpetuated that cats have nine lives, but one may suppose that the Khajiit indeed have not one but two. Scholars and the "True Cats" themselves assert that the Khajiiti soul possesses a duality, of a kind, that perhaps hearkens to the twin Sky Spirits, Jone and Jode. The two moon children, cradled by Khenarthi - or Kynareth - in their stillbirth, are said to dance in the Lunar Lattice; given life through praise, in form of song. Moonlight, dance, and song seem intrinsically tied to the path all Khajiit walk through this life. But not all dances are those of joy. The dro-m'Athra, or Bent Cats, are those who succumb to the "second life" - shadows growing long as the sound of drums beats in their heads, a dance without music that follows the rhythm of a fell imitation of the Heart of Lorkhaj. Lorkhaj himself is viewed as another duality: both as the enlightened favorite child of Fadomai, and as the dark Moon Beast corrupted by Namiira. [pagebreak] The first sign of such influence can manifest as strong pain, confusion, hearing voices in one's head - believed to be Namiira's own voice. Only Khajiit may become dro-m'Athra, but any race on Mundus may suffer these symptoms of the Bent Dance. My own mother, an Imperial advanced in her years, displays such symptoms so strongly she hears all voices but those she should love; thus am I moved to study the Dance and its root, that turns the world dark for so many. It is the Khajiit's unique duality of soul that allows them, however, to make a choice to succumb to the Heart. Some may fight valiantly, or resist without effort, whilst others may be predisposed to corruption by family line or use of skooma. Would that my mother could have made the choice to become lost in her mind, for I know she would never have chosen this, but willpower alone is rarely enough to truly deliver a soul from the Bent Dance. [pagebreak] While there is no saving a dro-m'Athra once turned, one may halt the transformation before its end by singing. This provides a chance for them to twist the tune to something pure and whole, thus returning them to their "first" life. I can personally attest to the healing that song has worked for my own mother: she remembers herself, and my face, when together we sing. The light comes back to her eyes, as if in defiance of Namiira's other name: The Great Darkness. So, though nine lives is too naive a tale to tell of the Khajiit, I do not believe it is to say that keeping a song in one's heart will keep the darkness at bay. Not forever, but for a time; and that time may just be enough for us to find new paths to the light. I can only hope my continued research into the dro-m'Athra allows me to find them.

[pagebreak]

String.Source: <font face="$HandwrittenBold" size="19"> As N. mentioned, the Ayleids of Varladimath do seem to have had a relationship with the ancient Cronvangr, but nothing of value seems to have come from it. These were not the expert mages of Varladimath's prime - the Cronvangr's contact was nothing but a cultist worshipping the memory of the Hollow Princess. The cultists' enchanting and alchemy tools were interesting, however. As with all items from Varladimath, I can feel the Void infusing them - a simple experiment with them was sufficient to open a breach here. Perhaps these tools will be what I need to craft the Vessel. If nothing else, the power absorbed from the breach will be useful in future experiments. </font>

String.Source:
<font face='$SkyrimBooks' size='18'> Most born in Tamriel will find themselves forever bound there, trapped within the mundane world until the day they die. Out of sympathy for those less magically inclined, the great mage Vilatri Thrad publishes the Voyages Through Oblivion series so that the reader may vicariously experience these other planes. Those wishing to further support these writings may send donations to the Dancing Draugr Inn. Please include a note authorizing the use of funds for Skooma purchase. [pagebreak] In this volume, Vilatri Thrad explores the demi-plane of The Old Lands. [pagebreak] Following my hasty exit from the Third Sinus of Takubar, and taking into account that I was still unwelcome in Detritus after my unwitting insult of Lord Hollowjack - and let it be known once more that my allergy to pumpkins was entirely beyond my control - I elected to stop at a plane closer to Tamriel, in appearance if not in nature.
The Old Lands, as its inhabitants call it (DOP 33910.23), is not considered a full plane of Oblivion but is rather a demi-plane located between Tamriel and DOP 29123.31. According to the legends passed down by its inhabitants - most of whom are migrants from Tamriel, not native daedra - the Old Lands was once a place within Mundus itself, said to be the spot where Lorkhan himself created Mundus (I believe this is related to the traditional Reachfolk creation myth, wherein the spirit Lorkh claimed a place within the Void for mortals to dwell). [pagebreak] Less fantastically, the bulk of the region appears to be a segment of land that was once located within the Reach (near Raven Spring, or Arnima as it is now known, judging by the geological similarities) before being pulled into Oblivion during the early Merethic Era. Other segments of the realm, such as the swampy western region, seem to be the result of artificial land-forming, though I am unsure who or what may have done this.
The locals of the Old Lands are an eclectic mix of Argonians, Khajiit, and Reachfolk, all of whom worship what they call "the Old Blood." This strange fluid seeps from the roots that grow throughout the realm and, according to local myth, is the last blood ever to flow from Lorkhan after the loss of his heart, before the Darkness filled the empty space. They believe that consuming the Blood grants them magical abilities and elevates their souls to the level of the primal spirits. Regrettably, my continued inability to open my mouth - lingering from the Demi-Prince of Pastries' curse during my visit to the Isles, which I have yet to find a way to break - prevented me from sampling the Blood myself. Perhaps next time. [pagebreak] The Aurbical alignment of the Old Lands is rather unique. Despite its close proximity to Tamriel - to this day, it can be accessed via a portal located in the Reach - anyone with magical sense would detect the strong influence of the Void here. During my stay, I witnessed several breaches in the fabric of reality, through which emerged a number of entities that even a daedra would consider alien. Thankfully, these beings did not notice me, as they were too busy dissolving into viscous slime. Even so, I would advise anyone visiting this realm to keep the Sacred Numbers in the forefront of their mind in case a more powerful entity from beyond the Aurbis were to take notice. </font>
String.Dest:

String.Source:
<font face="$HandwrittenBold" size="19"> The Dark Descent has long been a place where the clans of the Reach would commune with Namira. Even if the Forsworn claim sole ownership of it now, the magic in the depths still recognizes the blood of all who call the Reach home.
This would normally be a suitable place to attune the Vessel, but the constant interruptions from the Hagravens and their minions make it too risky. If the ritual were to fail due to an ill-timed interruption, all would be lost. Better to find an alternate site for the full attunement... Somewhere else tied to the Void. There are plenty of such gaps within the Reach. Perhaps I will have better luck with the ruins of Arkthzand... Surely one of the ruins near Deep Folk Crossing will have a working lift.
I will leave the breach here untouched for now. It may prove useful in the future. </font>

String.Source:
[pagebreak]

Manifestations of the Void by Daromeda Kathrus

[pagebreak]

The Spheres of aedra and daedra are such that any reasonably educated mortal could recite them. Julianos, patron of knowledge. Sheogorath, patron of madness. The Spheres of the Magna-Ge may be less known, but those who study such matters are at least aware of their fleeting spheres - the feeling that one has forgotten to tell a friend of an important matter, or the scientific motivation embodied by Mnethm. The Spheres of the Void Spirits, however, are less known than even those of the Magna-Ge, and for good reason: How can a being from outside reality, one with no connection at all to the Aurbis, embody a concept within reality? And yet they do, and for a deceptively simple reason: it is by thus embodying a concept that these spirits can manifest within the Aurbis at all. [pagebreak] To elaborate, there are, to my knowledge, three main ways a being from the Void may manifest in reality. The first method is simple brute force, pushing their way past the natural barriers of reality and into the Aurbis. Such methods rarely work, with all recorded instances of such attempts ending with the spirit in question ceasing to exist or being cast back into the Void in a short time. We should be glad this is the case, as anything powerful enough to truly force its way into reality would likely be the type to accidentally destroy reality in the process. Thankfully, this is purely theoretical. The second method by which a Void entity may manifest is by enlisting itself into the service of a native spirit - a daedra, generally. This is the most common method, and the most successful. Entities such as Namira and Nocturnal are known to command a great many such subservient entities - the Voidmothers and Shades of Namira, or the enigmatic Harrowing Reapers (known to serve both Namira and Nocturnal at times), for example. [pagebreak] The third method for a Void entity to manifest is that which I mentioned earlier: to claim a Sphere for themselves. In other words, the entity must seize control of some aspect of reality that has been discarded or otherwise left unattended, and warp this aspect into a novel form which then serves as a metaphysical anchor - a metanymic, in scholarly parlance - for the entity. This is what leads to the existence of those we call the Greater Void Spirits. By way of example, I offer several such Spirits: Kalarix Brood, Mother of Parasites, is a self-explanatory example. She has claimed a part of the Sphere of Decay embodied by Namira - with Namira's blessing, to the best of my knowledge - and made herself its embodiment, in much the way a Daedra Lord can claim the plane of a Prince, such as Hircine and the Demiprince of Fishing. Another example of this collaboration would be Millamaste the Golden, Patron of Self-Inflicted Loss of Control, whose Sphere consists of discarded elements from both Sanguine and Sheogorath. Ghyrax Bahn, patron of Obfuscation Through Loquaciousness, is an example of an entity that has taken possession of a normally Aedric concept, having warped a portion of Julianos' Sphere into his own distorted version. [pagebreak] Most such Greater Void Spirits embody such "warped" Spheres. Sondra Drel the Despondent, Patron of Hopelessness. Likirani, Patron of Radiance. Xibbenxaml, Patron of Pointless War. Varanix, Patron of those who Worship Luck. In fact, I can think of only two spirits who would not directly fit this description of a warped Sphere: My own master, Dame Murder, has no such Sphere, as she is not an outsider to the Aurbis at all. She was once a Listener of the Dark Brotherhood and was ascended to her current form within the Void as a blessing from Sithis and the Night Mother. In this respect, she could be considered analogous to those ascended by Namira or Nocturnal - though far superior, of course. The other outsider to this paradigm would, of course, be Anananis the Weaver, who does not exist within the Aurbis in a conventional form at all, but instead dwells within the Dreamsleeve. Those who know of such matters will already understand my meaning, and those who lack such understanding would be wise to not enquire in matters of the Dreamsleeve Spider any further.
String.Dest:

String.Source: 8th of Morning Star This one has finally arrived in the Old Lands. If Li'Rakka's taunt was true, this is where Namiira gathers the dro-m'Athra. This one does not know what Namiira is planning, nor does he care. This one vowed to see Li'Rakka freed from her torment, and that is what he will do. 15th of Morning Star Ri'nakkhu will handle scouting the southern parts of the desert, while this one scouts the north. There are many ruins here - the ancient Khajiit of the False Moon were ambitious, if nothing else. But this one will be as patient as he needs to be. He and Ri'nakkhu will search every ruin ourselves if we must. 2nd of Rain's Hand Living in the Old Lands is surprisingly comfortable. The land itself is harsh, but the people are kind. Li'Rakka would have liked it here. [pagebreak] 22nd of Sun's Height This one is feeling confident. He has narrowed down the potential ruins to four. - Seribani Sallidadna: "The Prison of Death." (Or perhaps "The place where the dead are shackled?" This one is unsure how much Ta'agra has changed since the False Moon cult came here in the early Second Era.) This seems to be a place where the dro-m'Athra torment the imprisoned souls of cats who refuse to join the Bent Dance. This one pities them, but this one also remembers how he used to play with the mice he caught as a child... - Aydithozay Zha'morna: "Dance of the Dreamless Dark" (this one thinks so, anyway. The grammar is a bit odd). This seems to be a temple where the False Moon worshipped Varmiina. This one was a bit surprised to learn that, since he had not heard of Varmiina being an ally of Namiira, but he supposes both are enemies of Azurah, and that is likely all the False Moon cared about. They did not seem very fond of her. This one is sleepy now. He will examine the other two ruins tomorrow. [pagebreak] 24th of Sun's Height The caravans from Tamriel arrived with Moon Sugar. This one overslept as a result of much sugar. He feels guilty now. Li'Rakka cannot enjoy the sugar with him. This one finished his studies of the other two ruins as penance. - Zhanlaj Zhanzalv: "Wind-Stalker's Rise." This one sometimes thinks Ta'agra has too many "zha" words. This ruin is as evil as the name sounds - the dro-m'Athra have performed some sort of ritual here to seal away Khenarthi's winds. No wonder the winds of the desert are so harsh, if Khenarthi cannot bring her healing breeze to this realm. The dro-m'Athra are truly cruel. - Laj'dadna: "The mountain of death." This is an odd one. This one was not expecting to find a dro-m'Athra lair so close to the swamp. It is quite distant from the other ruins - perhaps the False Moon once had ambitions to push out the Argonians and colonize the xanmeers as well? This one thinks that is a foolish idea. Khajiit and swamp water do not mix. Li'Rakka is likely in one of these four. This one will need to investigate further - and find ways to weaken the forces of the dro-m'Athra so they cannot interfere with his rescue mission.

They did not seem very fond of her. This one is sleepy now. He will examine the other two ruins tomorrow. [pagebreak] 24th of Sun's Height The caravans from Tamriel arrived with Moon Sugar. This one overslept as a result of much sugar. He feels guilty now. Li'Rakka cannot enjoy the sugar with him. This one finished his studies of the other two ruins as penance. - Zhanlaj Zhanzalv: "Wind-Stalker's Rise." This one sometimes thinks Ta'agra has too many "zha" words. This ruin is as evil as the name sounds - the dro-m'Athra have performed some sort of ritual here to seal away Khenarthi's winds. No wonder the winds of the desert are so harsh, if Khenarthi cannot bring her healing breeze to this realm. The dro-m'Athra are truly cruel. - Laj'dadna: "The mountain of death." This is an odd one. This one was not expecting to find a dro-m'Athra lair so close to the swamp. It is quite distant from the other ruins - perhaps the False Moon once had ambitions to push out the Argonians and colonize the xanmeers as well? This one thinks that is a foolish idea. Khajiit and swamp water do not mix. Li'Rakka is likely in one of these four. This one will need to investigate further - and find ways to weaken the forces of the dro-m'Athra so they cannot interfere with his rescue mission.

String.Source: <font face="$HandwrittenBold" size="19"> Damnation! I had hoped to use the old Nalzthdbar Great Lift to reach the Arkthzand Library, but once again fate conspires against me. Nearly the entirely of the Nalzthdbar ruins have collapsed, the same as the ruins of Bthar-Zel. It seems Arkthzand is truly inaccessible... I will need to find an alternate way of attuning the Vessel to the Heart after all. Perhaps I can harness enough Void energy in the parts of Blackreach that remain accessible... The Lightless Hollow, potentially? Or perhaps I can find some other rift within the Reach that still links to Namira's realm. Either way, I refuse to accept failure. I am so close to completing the Vessel, I know it. </font>

String.Source: <font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'> I apologize if this letter is an inconvenience to you, but I wish to inform you of a change at the Church. Following your success in ringing the bell, Zenkali-Dra seems to have begun contemplating her own role in the future of the Church. As such, she has recently departed from the Church of the Old Blood to perform a pilgrimage across the Old Lands. Until such time as she returns, I have taken over her duties as leader of the Church. Should you have the time, I would be grateful for any assistance you can provide. My new duties have shown me that a great many tasks must be done if the Church is to survive, and I fear I cannot achieve them all myself. Ancheta </font>

String.Source:
[pagebreak]

Jokes of Daggerfall by Butha Sunhous

[pagebreak]

"How is your wife?" asked Zalither. "She's in bed with laryngitis," replied Harlyth. "Is that Argonian bastard back in town again?" ~~~~~ "I keep seeing spots before my eyes." "Have you seen a healer?" "No, just spots." ~~~~~ A big Nord named Julgen was set on by a gang of thieves. He fought them furiously, but in the end, they beat him into semiconsciousness. They searched his pockets and discovered that he only had three gold pieces on him. "Do you mean to tell us you fought us like a mad lupe for three lousy gold pieces?" sneered one of the thieves. "No," answered Julgen. "I was afraid you were after the four hundred gold pieces in my boot." [pagebreak] During the War of Betony, the Bretons in the Isle of Craghold were under siege for several days. After the island was liberated, Lord Bridwell found the ruins of the castle where a crowd of survivors were hidden away in the dark. It was going to be a difficult job freeing them, as part of the roof had collapsed trapping them all within. Bridwell stuck his head in the only opening and shouted to the Bretons below: "Are there any expectant mothers down there?" "It's hard to say, your Lordship," said a young woman. "We've only been down here for a few days." ~~~~~ An elderly Breton met with a contemporary of his at a guild meeting. "Harryston, old man, I wanted to express my sympathy. I hear that you buried your wife last week." "Had to, old boy," replied Harryston. "Dead, you know." ~~~~~ Why was the Sentinel navy so useless during the War of Betony? The cannons were too heavy, so all three garbage scows sunk. ~~~~~ What does a new Sentinel private learn first as a combat technique? How to retreat. ~~~~~ What is the thinnest book in the world? Redguard Heroes of the War of Betony. ~~~~~ A Dark Elf man killed his wife after catching her making love with another man. When the magistrate asked him why he killed her instead of her lover, the man replied, "I considered it better to kill one woman than a different man every week." ~~~~~ A Dark Elf woman was being shown around Daggerfall. When she was shown the magnificent Castle Daggerfall, she smiled sweetly to her guide and whispered, "It reminds me of sex." "That's odd," said her guide. "Why does our Castle Daggerfall remind you of sex?" The Dark Elf sighed, "Everything does." ~~~~~ Yelithah told Vathysah that she was having dinner with a Dark Elf named Morleth that night. "I hear he's an animal," said Vathysah. "He'll rip your dress right off you." "Thank you for telling me," said Yelithah, "I'll be sure to wear an old dress." ~~~~~ How do you separate sailors in the Khajiiti navy? With a hammer and tongs. ~~~~~ "This orchard has sentimental value to me," said Mojhad, the Khajiit, to his friend, Hasillid. "Under that tree, for example, is where I first made love. And that tree, is where her mother stood, watching us." "She watched you while you made love to her daughter?" said Hasillid, clearly impressed. "Didn't she say anything?" "Meow." ~~~~~ What do you call a Wood Elf who doesn't lie or cheat or steal? A dead Wood Elf.

String.Source: <font face="$HandwrittenBold" size="19"> I had hoped to use Lightless Hollow as a route into the lost library of Arkthzand, but it seems the passage of time has stymied me once again. While the rifts in reality remain, any direct connection to Arkthzand proper seems to have faded. The most I was able to access was this research annex. The Dwemer writings here are unintelligible to me, but I may still be able to make use of this - this annex is partially drifting within the Void and thus may provide a partial link to the remnants of the Dark Heart's energy. If I am able to attune it, I can use this annex to channel more Void energy into the workshop I've set up in Lightless Hollow. This may be just what I need to complete the Vessel. </font>

String.Source: While ingesting the Blood raises us closer to the ancient Spirits, it is the duty of those in the Church to ensure that the Blood is taken appropriately. Lack of sufficient Blood can make one become Dryblood, but consumption in excess can overwhelm the soul as well. The following guidelines can help to ensure that the appropriate ministration is provided. 1: Always ingest, never inject. Direct replacement of mortal blood with divine Blood, absent the mediating influence of the stomach, is more than the soul can handle, and will result in seizures and death. 2: Children and the elderly receive smaller doses, as their bodies cannot handle the same degree of magic as a healthy adult. 3: No more than two doses per week! If the worshipper begins feeling the pangs of withdrawal between doses, this can be mediated via consumption of Meat from the mines in the swamp. Meat is no substitute for Blood, but regularly consuming it can alleviate the cravings.

String.Source: <font face='$HandwrittenFont'>Pardon the interruption - I'm sure your duties to the Quarra Clan are keeping you quite occupied, but I have information I believe may be of use to you. Have you heard of the Voidsucker Clan? Or perhaps their more common name, the "Old-Blood Vampires?" They are a rather unusual clan of vampires and rely on an equally unusual source of blood. Regrettably, they are also violent savages, and I hear they have begun probing into Skyrim of late. Their involvement could jeopardize other vampire clans... including the Quarra. If you consider this matter to be worth your attention, I suggest you begin by investigating Twisted Root Cave at the base of the Karthspire. And, if you require assistance, seek out Capiton Esdrescus, an agent of mine currently investigating the Voidsuckers. Show him this note, and he will be obligated to assist. -VC

String.Source:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'> I apologize for sending this as a note rather than saying it to your face. Perhaps I've yet to overcome my cowardice, but I wished to let you know my thoughts, even if I couldn't find the words in person.
Zenkali-Dra was a mentor to me. She raised me, trained me in the ways of the Church. Perhaps you saw no trace of warmth in her, but I still remember the days she showed me kindness. Yet at the same time, I cannot begrudge you your actions. Much as I mourn my mentor, I confess I mainly mourn the version I remember from childhood. As the Blood dried, Zenkali-Dra fell further away from who she once was. A woman who once tried to aid everyone became a recluse, paranoid that everyone was plotting against her. She bared her claws against me more than once as well.
Perhaps your actions were for the best. I saw the signs of the Dryblood in her eyes - or perhaps the despair that leads Khajiit to become dro-m'Athra. I could do nothing but placate her in hopes that it would keep her from losing herself, but I know it was pointless. Much as I mourn her loss, I can console myself that at least her body ended before her soul. She will not be forced to wander as a mad ghost or serve as one of the Bent Cats.
All this is to say what I could not when we spoke. I do not blame you for your actions - you did what you believed was right to aid the miners. You were only defending yourself from Zenkali-Dra's fury. Know that, despite everything, you are still welcome in the Church of the Old Blood. I will do my best to be the type of priestess the people need, and your help would be most appreciated. Please feel free to come to the Church if you wish to help.
Ancheta </font>

String.Source: <font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'> - Unusual religion here. Was expecting daedra worship, but the locals seem to believe they're worshipping Lorkhan? - Basics of faith: Drinking "Blood" from roots (they think this is the Blood of Lorkhan? Concerning. Can I get a sample of this to Ciirta for Raelynne to study?). They think this will move them "closer to the Spirits." Seems like a modified version of Reach myth about Tamriel being a testing ground for spirits. - Khajiit here are mostly descended from survivors of a Namira cult. No Namira worship remains among the modern Khajiit - if anything, they seem to not practice any religion at all. Rejection of the Riddle'Thar is unusual for Khajiit, but I suppose not unheard of. - Argonians here mine "Meat" from the xanmeer ruins. Concerning that the locals don't find this unusual. Need to get a sample of this "Meat" for analysis. ~~~~ - Heard from Raelynne. The Blood sample decayed before she could analyze it. Seems to only retain its shape while in the Old Lands. - Analysis of Meat was more successful, but the results are vague. Seems to be standard meat, origin unknown, but infused with Chaotic Creatia. Surprising it can be consumed safely, especially considering how vulnerable Argonians in particular are to such influences. Raelynne noted an additional unidentified compound within the Meat - perhaps that acts as a mitigating factor to nullify the influence of the Creatia. - Was the Meat an object of worship for the ancient Argonians? Was it something they feared and sealed away? If only I could study the xanmeers in more depth, but the dangers are too great. ~~~~ - Conclusion thus far: Locals are not active daedra worshippers. In many cases, they seem to oppose the Princes, such as their efforts to push back the dro-m'Athra. Purging the villagers would not weaken the daedra, and could even strengthen their influence by removing forces that oppose them. Best option seems to be gentle guidance - keep the locals safe and alive, and hopefully help steer them away from their misguided Blood worship and to a more standard form of Lorkhan cult. - Additional concern: the cave near the village seems to contain a shrine of Kalarix Brood. The entrance is sealed, but its mere existence is a cause for worry - is there an active Void cult somewhere in these lands? </font>

String.Source: My Vateshran has summoned me back to Skyrim. It has been decades since I've seen my homeland, but my services are needed. The clan requires my arcane knowledge to help drive away the Nords who slaughtered our people. The disruption to my research is irritating, but I may be able to use this to my advantage. If I play my cards right, perhaps I can convince Vateshran Iorus to grant me access to the Old Lands...
String.Dest: My Vateshran has summoned me back to Skyrim. It has been decades since I've seen my homeland, but my services are needed. The clan requires my arcane knowledge to help drive away the Nords who slaughtered our people. The disruption to my research is irritating, but I may be able to use this to my advantage. If I play my cards right, perhaps I can convince Vateshran Iorus to grant me access to the Old Lands...

String.Source: Vateshran Iorus finally embraced my idea. The power of the Old Lands has been a legend to our people for eons, but to venture within and claim the power has always been taboo. But now, with the Forsworn being driven back, Iorus finally sees the need for true power - and the foolishness of allowing ancient superstitions to stand in our way. Of course, the arguments I used weren't entirely my own, but what N doesn't know won't hurt him. It's his own fault for wasting all his time with that Glass cult of his up in Cyrodiil instead of taking the initiative.

String.Source: After some weeks of study, I've reached a revelation. The "Old Blood" is indeed the blood of a godlike being, though not the one these fools believe. An ancient Hist Tree, mutated by exposure to the Void. From what I've gathered based on local legends and my own studies, I believe I see what happened here: The Old Lands were indeed once part of the Reach. Back in the Merethic Era, some Argonain cultists brought a Hist sapling here and planted it in the caverns above where Namira's Dark Heart slept. After centuries of feeding on the energies of the Heart, the Hist used the power to sever the Old Lands from Tamriel and create its own demiplane where it could continue to grow. The "Meat" excavated from the swamps supports this connection to Namira - it closely resembles the "fleshy ground" known to compose much of Namira's Scuttling Void. It seems the Hist sap has soaked into this material, creating the "Meat" the locals use to augment their "Blood" consumption. Despite being physically separated, the Hist continued feeding on the Heart's power until the Gray Host incident in the Second Era - meaning for thousands and thousands of years, this godlike tree absorbed the raw power of the Void. And in using its mutant sap - its "Blood" - to spread its influence to the cultists, the tree has unwittingly Mantled the Dark Heart itself. All those fools who wanted the power within the Blood are missing the true potential here: a new Dark Heart, the Heart of the Mountain. A true embodiment of the Void, just waiting to be claimed.
String.Dest: After some weeks of study, I've reached a revelation. The "Old Blood" is indeed the blood of a godlike being, though not the one these fools believe. An ancient Hist Tree, mutated by exposure to the Void. From what I've gathered based on local legends and my own studies, I believe I see what happened here: The Old Lands were indeed once part of the Reach. String.Source: Damn it all! The Hist must have sensed my attempts to siphon its power - it entirely severed the roots connecting itself to the village! Now I no longer have any access to the tree - and worse, the villagers here will soon go mad without access to their precious "Blood," which will make it even more difficult to conduct research! I'll need to reach the Hist directly, but that damn ancient Ayleid did too good a job sealing it off. Were I a younger man, perhaps I'd be able to infiltrate the Hollow Palace myself, but my body no longer cooperates. I'll need to find an alternative method...

String.Source: Leaving the Old Lands and setting up a research station in Blackreach was the right choice. It took several years and countless failures, but the Vessel is complete. The principle of Mantling was the correct choice. The flaw in the original Numidium was simple - the Dwemer were a race of nihilists, but the power source they chose for their Tower, the Heart of Lorkhan, was a power of creation, not destruction. My Vessel's creation mimics the process used in the creation of Numidium as best I could, albeit substituting Reach magic for Tonal Architecture, but with a key distinction: I will use the new Dark Heart as the power source. With the Void as the Vessel's core, my new Numidium will be stable... and as its master, I will remake the Aurbis in my own image.

String.Source: Irritatingly, the Vessel seems to have attained self-awareness. Perhaps the spells I used to attune it with the Dark Heart allowed some Void entity to slip through as well. It shouldn't pose much of an issue - my command spells still ensure the Vessel can't go against the directives I've imposed. Breach the Hollow Palace, absorb the Heart of the Mountain, then return to me so that I may begin the process of rewriting reality. Even so, I will need to prepare a backup plan, just in case this Vessel decides to keep the power for itself...

Hana the Wanderer, Book 1

[pagebreak] Hana was a child of stone and jungle, born under the sign of the Un-Stars. They spoke to her in her dreams, weaving visions of lands she had never seen. Lands of stone and fire, of sand and salt, of crystal and flesh. And when she awoke, she spoke of these lands to those around her, and the wise travelers nodded at her words, for they had visited these lands themselves. And when Hana came of age, she was given a bottle of starlight and a cloak of souls, and the wise travelers guided her to the lands of her dreams.
String.Dest:
[pagebreak]

String.Source: My colleagues in the Order of the Eye believe the Old Lands are not worth our time to deal with. They claim I overestimate the influence of the Void seeping in or that Namira lacks the ambitions of the more dangerous Princes. They tell me to worry about more immediate dangers like the Cult of Sybandis or the Red Lotus. They are fools. The slow, gradual nature of the Old Lands is the very reason for its danger. The Hollow Princess has been using the power of the realm to harvest the magic of the Void since the Merethic Era! They believe that, because she has not acted yet, it means she never will. They miss the obvious: She - and more importantly, Namira - are waiting. The Old Lands not only freely draw on the power of the Void; they are linked directly to The Reach, bypassing the barriers placed by the Divines. The Hollow Palace is a storehouse of incredible magic, and, once it has absorbed enough, they will release it all at once. A wave of death far worse than any the world has seen from the likes of Dagon or Bal. A Harrowstorm to cover all of Nirn. I do not know when they will have gathered enough power to do this. It may be within a year. It may not be for another ten millennia. What does time matter to a being from beyond? Either way, I cannot allow this threat to continue. If I do not put an end to it, the blood of the future victims will be on my hands. Bypassing the barriers around the Palace nearly exhausted my strength, but I cannot surrender. The Hollow Princess must fall.

Hana the Wanderer, Book 2

[pagebreak] Hana came upon a desert where the sand was made of sugar, and cats danced upon the dunes. And Hana saw that the cats danced with such vigor that their shadows could not keep up. "Why do you dance so madly?" she asked. "If our dance slows, the shadows will catch up to us," the lead cat answered. And he danced with such fury that the ground could not keep up, and the cat flew up to the moons. "Perhaps next time," Hana said, "you should let the shadows lead."

Hana the Wanderer, Book 3

[pagebreak] Hana came upon a swamp where stone faces gazed down on old trees, and lizards wove music from sap and memories. And the lizards poured blood upon the stones, blood so thick that Time could not push through. "A stone is valuable because of its age," Hana said, "otherwise we would have no diamonds, only coal." And Sithis crept into the stone faces and drank up all the blood, and thus the lizards could see their shadows cast against the stones once more, and saw themselves. And the lizards rejoiced, and wove their songs into Hana's dress of memories, where it mingled with the starlight and carried her onward.

Hana the Wanderer, Book 4

[pagebreak] Hana came upon a lake where the water was clear as glass and still as ice. And she saw the stars reflected within the lake, and beyond them, she saw what the starlight hid. And the things that were not stars whispered through the darkness, begging to be seen. Hana did not fear these things, for she knew their nature, and that nature was potential. She loosened her bottle of light upon the lake, and the things in the dark were illuminated, and they came down to speak with her. Lesser travelers could not comprehend, and they dove into the lake and became still. But Hana spoke with the darkness, and thus was enlightened.
