Hana the Wanderer, Book 5

[pagebreak] Hana came upon a land of cold mountains, where shadows covered the light and brass churned below the ground. And the men in the hills knew Hana and sat her by their fire, and fed her flesh of the creatures that grazed in the shadows. "This mountain is the world," the men told her, "and the world is this mountain. The shadows are blood and blood is made of darkness, and that is right and proper. We choose where to shine our lights, and where we shine them, the mountain grows. Without the darkness, there is nowhere to grow." And Hana shone her starlight into the darkness, and the mountain opened its mouth for her.

String.Source: <font face="$HandwrittenBold" size="19"> I had hoped that studying the Eldergleam would provide some useful information for manipulating similar magical trees such as the Hist, but no suck luck. The Hist are unique, and Namira's influence has made that even more true. Nothing I've learned here will help me to take control of the Hist, though that is a worthwhile discovery in its own right: trying to sieze the Hist itself is futile. Better to destroy it and wrench the magic of the Dark Heart from its remains. As for this corrupted replica of the Eldergleam Sanctuary created (or, perhaps, revealed?) by my experiments, I will leave it as-is for now. It could be useful in the future. </font>

String.Source: <font face='$HandwrittenFont'> My dear knight, I have wonderful news. While my reliance on the "Old Blood" has not been completely resolved, my mage contact was able to brew up a sufficient replacement for me from a combination of a standard Blood Potion and some Hist Sap imported from Black Marsh. As I now have quite a large supply of this to use while I wean myself off of the reliance on Hist Sap entirely, I feel comfortable venturing out of the forest - besides, it's rather lonely here. Should you ever desire a traveling companion, please come visit - I would be delighted to accompany you. Yours, Kalsesh Darkbiter

String.Source: <font face="$HandwrittenBold" size="19"> Seeking wisdom on Void Magic from existing scholarly research has proved frustrating. What little work I've managed to find on the matter is either incoherent nonsense or irrelevant babble by worshippers of specific Void Spirits. It seems the Psijics have indeed managed to hide away any research of actual value. Thankfully, they have not eliminated the knowledge of the Void passed down by the tribes of the Reach. That will suffice as a starting point. </font>
String.Dest: <font face="$HandwrittenBold" size="19"> Seeking wisdom on Void Magic from existing scholarly research has proved frustrating. What little work I've managed to find on the matter is either incoherent nonsense or irrelevant babble by worshippers of specific Void Spirits. It seems the Psijics have indeed managed to hide away any research of actual value. Thankfully, they have not eliminated the knowledge of the Void passed down by the tribes of the Reach. That will suffice as a starting point. </font>

String.Source:
[pagebreak]

Studies of the Void: Jhavix Aihn

[pagebreak] Of the namable Greater Void Spirits, one of the most mysterious is Jhavix Aihn, "The Deep." No records of his summoning exist that I could determine, and even the students of Void magic that agreed to speak with me (though most, I admit, still attempted to sacrifice me afterward) said only that he had no interest in the "land dwellers." [pagebreak] As interviewing a Sload was beyond what I could stomach, and as any attempt to locate representatives of Hahd and/or Nahd has resulted only in laughter and accusations of being a madman, I elected to interview a group of civilized Dreugh. These Dreugh confirmed that they had indeed witnessed temples to Jhavix Aihn in the deepest of abyssal trenches, though they had never entered those regions themselves out of a fear of "another war with the Eyeless Ones." (No clarification was provided.) While they had never interacted with cultists or relics of Jhavix Aihn themselves, the Dreugh representatives I questioned explained that Aihn is a patron spirit focused primarily on "Rectangular Concepts." When pressed for clarification, they were unable to provide a direct explanation. They did, however, offer several examples of such concepts, including tuning forks, the sound of undercooked sea urchins, and the number nineteen. It should, at this point, be apparent to the reader why I chose to end my research into this topic.
String.Dest:
[pagebreak]

Revised Compiled Reports on the Clans of Skyrim 4E 198

[pagebreak] The Volkihar: Lord Harkon continues to pursue his prophecy, blind to the metaphysical and practical ramifications of blocking out the sun. Clan Volkihar has begun growing bolder in recent months, with some reports of brazen attacks on mortal regional capitals. This is unacceptable. The current situation requires the prey to be unaware of vampiric activity. Should Harkon persist in his mad obsession with prophecy, he must be disposed of. Unfortunately, the strength - and political power among other clans - of the Volkihar prevent direct action against the clan as a whole for now. I recommend a twofold approach - elimination of Harkon while retaining the overall power structure of the Volkihar and the insertion of Vampyrum agents into the advisorship of his replacement. Barring this, subtly strengthening local vampire-hunting organizations may be necessary. ADDENDUM: We have been unable to make contact with Agent Goldwynne. At present, we must conclude that the Volkihar uncovered her subterfuge and disposed of her. Monitoring of Skyrim clans has been transferred to Agent Caerellia. Revised recommendation is to remain distant and observe until an opportunity presents itself. [pagebreak] The Cronvangr: Historical notes indicate the Cronvangr spider-cultists ruled over the Old Holds for the majority of the Third Era but were significantly weakened during the Oblivion Crisis. Reports are unclear, but it appears a high-ranking Cronvangr attempted to defect and form his own clan, resulting in the deaths of many clan members. Since then, the clan has found itself challenged by numerous upstarts, primarily the Quarra. The current leader of the clan is Vlkoslak, a traditionalist who may be receptive to our agenda if his ego can be appeased. [pagebreak] The Quarra: Formerly a Vvardenfell clan under the leadership of Volrina Quarra, the Quarra Clan was forced to flee to Skyrim shortly following the Red Year. Since then, they have been primarily engaged in a violent feud with the Cronvangr. I speculate that this enmity is due to similarity in the philosophies of the Cronvangr and the historical rivals of the Quarra, the Berne. Despite their rather unstable position, the Quarra have managed to secure a reasonable territory for themselves, likely as a result of their relationship with the Volkihar. This creates an unusual situation - while their current leader, Clanlord Jelkar, is in many ways a vassal of the Volkihar, he is also directly indebted to Agent Caerellia due to her involvement in the clan's escape from Vvardenfell. These conflicting loyalties may be beneficial if we can maneuver him properly. [pagebreak] ADDENDUM: the Clan-Feud: At present, the Cronvangr Clan is occupied feuding with the Quarra Clan. Despite nearly two centuries, neither clan has gained a clear advantage. As a result, the areas of Skyrim outside of Volkihar control currently have no clear leader. Should this persist, we risk Skyrim fracturing into a vampiric civil war, with every clan attempting to stake out new territory. As our Lord's plans require stability in the region, this situation must be resolved before it escalates to the point of chaos. Two possibilities are present: either one of the clans must be firmly established as the victor of the feud and made into a stabilizing influence in the region or both must be eliminated so that the lesser clans can be cowed. Agent Caerellia is currently examining the situation and will make a final determination on how to proceed. Until then, all other agents are instructed to avoid contact with both clans. [pagebreak] Movarth Piquine: Despite earlier reports indicating his death, we have confirmed that the hunter-turned-vampire remains active. Turning him may have been in error - rather than joining the Order, he has instead formed his own clan and is attempting to gather new minions. Recommend continued observation to determine whether he can be converted into a proper vassal or if he must be eliminated before he can become a rival. Morgus Ghoruun: Previously the dominant independent clanlord in the Morthal region, Ghoruun was displaced by Movarth Piquine at some point during the Third Era, though the exact date of this usurpation is unclear. Subsequent reports suggest he may have moved to the Hjorkvild Archipelago or another island in the Sea of Ghosts, though no confirmed observations have occured in recent centuries. As such, Morgus Ghoruun is included here for the sake of completeness only. [pagebreak] Vighar the Bloodletter: A cursory examination of Vighar's former lair in the Bloodlet Throne has confirmed his continued absence. So long as the wardstone remains over his grave in Falkreath, we do not foresee any issues with the remnants of Vighar's clan. The Wolf-Queen's Cult: Several vampires within the Solitude region appear to be planning a ritual to resurrect the Wolf-Queen. While the dominant clan in Solitude is unlikely to permit this, it is worth observation. Potema was an eager ally of the Vampyrum Order during her initial reign, so her resurrection could enable far greater access to resources in the region. Sybille Stentor: Redacted by request. Any inquiries should be directed to Agent Caerellia. [pagebreak] The Mother: An offshoot of the more vicious Scions of Lamae, the followers of Mother Laradyth appear to have migrated to Skyrim from Morrowind after an unclear incident. Our Lord has decreed that her heretical opposition to Molag Bal poses a risk to the vampires of Tamriel if it is allowed to spread. Agents have been dispatched to deal with the matter. The Berne: Following the Red Year, the Berne Clan has relocated to Solstheim and has been working to establish the entire island as their territory. While no other vampire clans of note are active on the island, the Berne are still encountering significant resistance from local werebears. Additionally, the clan continues to waste resources in strikes against the Quarra in Skyrim. As long as Clanlady Restita's obsessive grudge against the Quarra continues to guide her actions, the Berne are unlikely to regain their prior position of power. At present, they are not considered either a threat or a potential asset and are best ignored. [pagebreak] The Voidsuckers: While not directly located within Skyrim, members of the Voidsucker Clan occasionally venture out of their lair in the demi-plane of the Old Lands to prey upon the mortals of Skyrim. The clan is believed to have originated from a Nighthollow survivor of the Gray Host incident - a regrettable oversight. As our Lord has decreed that no remnants of the Nighthollow Clan can be allowed to exist, this oversight is to be corrected forthwith. The Dreameaters: The result of a Vaermina cult being infected with vampirism from Cronvangr defectors, the Dreameater's primary ambition appears to be to harness the nightmares known to afflict weak-minded vampires for their own ends. Their exact headquarters is unknown as of now but is likely in the vicinity of the cult's former temple, known as Syncope Sanctuary. As a scholar of Vaermina herself, Agent Caerellia has stated her intention to investigate the Dreameaters personally and will determine the optimal method for taking advantage of them. [pagebreak] Additonal notes: - Unconfirmed reports of independent vampires within the ruins of Old Windhelm, suspected to be a Lamae cult. Agent Caerellia does not foresee this cult's activities of having any relevance for our ambitions, and as such they are to be disregarded.

Unfortunately, the strength - and political power among other clans - of the Volkihar prevent direct action against the clan as a whole for now. I recommend a twofold approach - elimination of Harkon while retaining the overall power structure of the Volkihar and the insertion of Vampyrum agents into the advisorship of his replacement. Barring this, subtly strengthening local vampire-hunting organizations may be necessary. ADDENDUM: We have been unable to make contact with Agent Goldwynne. At present, we must conclude that the Volkihar uncovered her subterfuge and disposed of her. Monitoring of Skyrim clans has been transferred to Agent Caerellia. Revised recommendation is to remain distant and observe until an opportunity presents itself. [pagebreak] The Cronvangr: Historical notes indicate the Cronvangr spider-cultists ruled over the Old Holds for the majority of the Third Era but were significantly weakened during the Oblivion Crisis. Reports are unclear, but it appears a high-ranking Cronvangr attempted to defect and form his own clan, resulting in the deaths of many clan members. Since then, the clan has found itself challenged by numerous upstarts, primarily the Quarra. The current leader of the clan is Vlkoslak, a traditionalist who may be receptive to our agenda if his ego can be appeased. [pagebreak] The Quarra: Formerly a Vvardenfell clan under the leadership of Volrina Quarra, the Quarra Clan was forced to flee to Skyrim shortly following the Red Year. Since then, they have been primarily engaged in a violent feud with the Cronvangr. I speculate that this enmity is due to similarity in the philosophies of the Cronvangr and the historical rivals of the Quarra, the Berne. Despite their rather unstable position, the Quarra have managed to secure a reasonable territory for themselves, likely as a result of their relationship with the Volkihar. This creates an unusual situation - while their current leader, Clanlord Jelkar, is in many ways a vassal of the Volkihar, he is also directly indebted to Agent Caerellia due to her involvement in the clan's escape from Vvardenfell. These conflicting loyalties may be beneficial if we can maneuver him properly. [pagebreak] ADDENDUM: the Clan-Feud: At present, the Cronvangr Clan is occupied feuding with the Quarra Clan. Despite nearly two centuries, neither clan has gained a clear advantage. As a result, the areas of Skyrim outside of Volkihar control currently have no clear leader. Should this persist, we risk Skyrim fracturing into a vampiric civil war, with every clan attempting to stake out new territory. As our Lord's plans require stability in the region, this situation must be resolved before it escalates to the point of chaos. Two possibilities are present: either one of the clans must be firmly established as the victor of the feud and made into a stabilizing influence in the region or both must be eliminated so that the lesser clans can be cowed. Agent Caerellia is currently examining the situation and will make a final determination on how to proceed. Until then, all other agents are instructed to avoid contact with both clans. [pagebreak] Movarth Piquine: Despite earlier reports indicating his death, we have confirmed that the hunter-turned-vampire remains active. Turning him may have been in error - rather than joining the Order, he has instead formed his own clan and is attempting to gather new minions. Recommend continued observation to determine whether he can be converted into a proper vassal or if he must be eliminated before he can become a rival. Morgus Ghoruun: Previously the dominant independent clanlord in the Morthal region, Ghoruun was displaced by Movarth Piquine at some point during the Third Era, though the exact date of this usurpation is unclear. Subsequent reports suggest he may have moved to the Hjorkvild Archipelago or another island in the Sea of Ghosts, though no confirmed observations have occured in recent centuries. As such, Morgus Ghoruun is included here for the sake of completeness only. [pagebreak] Vighar the Bloodletter: A cursory examination of Vighar's former lair in the Bloodlet Throne has confirmed his continued absence. So long as the wardstone remains over his grave in Falkreath, we do not foresee any issues with the remnants of Vighar's clan. The Wolf-Queen's Cult: Several vampires within the Solitude region appear to be planning a ritual to resurrect the Wolf-Queen. While the dominant clan in Solitude is unlikely to permit this, it is worth observation. Potema was an eager ally of the Vampyrum Order during her initial reign, so her resurrection could enable far greater access to resources in the region. Sybille Stentor: Redacted by request. Any inquiries should be directed to Agent Caerellia. [pagebreak] The Mother: An offshoot of the more vicious Scions of Lamae, the followers of Mother Laradyth appear to have migrated to Skyrim from Morrowind after an unclear incident. Our Lord has decreed that her heretical opposition to Molag Bal poses a risk to the vampires of Tamriel if it is allowed to spread. Agents have been dispatched to deal with the matter. The Berne: Following the Red Year, the Berne Clan has relocated to Solstheim and has been working to establish the entire island as their territory. While no other vampire clans of note are active on the island, the Berne are still encountering significant resistance from local werebears. Additionally, the clan continues to waste resources in strikes against the Quarra in Skyrim. As long as Clanlady Restita's obsessive grudge against the Quarra continues to guide her actions, the Berne are unlikely to regain their prior position of power. At present, they are not considered either a threat or a potential asset and are best ignored. [pagebreak] The Voidsuckers: While not directly located within Skyrim, members of the Voidsucker Clan occasionally venture out of their lair in the demi-plane of the Old Lands to prey upon the mortals of Skyrim. The clan is believed to have originated from a Nighthollow survivor of the Gray Host incident - a regrettable oversight. As our Lord has decreed that no remnants of the Nighthollow Clan can be allowed to exist, this oversight is to be corrected forthwith. The Dreameaters: The result of a Vaermina cult being infected with vampirism from Cronvangr defectors, the Dreameater's primary ambition appears to be to harness the nightmares known to afflict weak-minded vampires for their own ends. Their exact headquarters is unknown as of now but is likely in the vicinity of the cult's former temple, known as Syncope Sanctuary. As a scholar of Vaermina herself, Agent Caerellia has stated her intention to investigate the Dreameaters personally and will determine the optimal method for taking advantage of them. [pagebreak] Additonal notes: - Unconfirmed reports of independent vampires within the ruins of Old Windhelm, suspected to be a Lamae cult. Agent Caerellia does not foresee this cult's activities of having any relevance for our ambitions, and as such they are to be disregarded.

String.Source:
[pagebreak]

Harrowstorms: Scourge of the Second Era Arcturius Clemens, Scribe

[pagebreak] While nearly a decade has passed since the Oblivion Crisis, the scars still run deep across Tamriel. Many wonder whether there is any hope at all of recovery. While I make no claim to the gift of foresight, I possess the gift of knowledge - the knowledge of history. And history makes me confident that we shall recover from this crisis, just as we have all such crises in the past. To highlight this, let me provide the example of a similar Daedric plot that occurred in the Second Era. Not the Planemeld - better scholars than I have written on that before - but an event that happened shortly after: The Harrowstorms of the Gray Host. The Gray Host (or rather, the second such army to use that name), for those not versed in obscure history, was an army of the undead - vampires, werewolves, and the like - led by a powerful vampire named Rada al-Saran, which rampaged across Skyrim shortly after the events of the Planemeld. Rada al-Saran sought to take advantage of Molag Bal's weakness after his defeat at the end of the Planemeld to free himself and his fellow vampires from their eternal imprisonment in Coldharbour. A sympathetic motive, perhaps, but their methods were as foul as any devised by Bal himself: The Harrowstorms. [pagebreak] A Harrowstorm is a magical storm that manifests suddenly in response to a magical ritual (invented, according to my research, by a coven of witches known as the Icereach Coven, though I suspect they may have merely rediscovered an older ritual), summoned by a magical focus. Upon manifesting, the storm exerts a magical pull on the souls of all living things within its radius. Weaker animals perish instantly, while stronger sapients can resist for a short time. However, the longer the storm persists, the larger it grows, and the stronger its pull. Given enough time, all mortals within the storm's radius will have their souls ripped from their bodies and absorbed by the focus of the storm, leaving them as nothing but mindless, vicious Harrowfiends. [pagebreak] That is the nature of what the Gray Host unleashed: massive Harrowstorms, all across Skyrim, with a particular focus on the Reach. They sought to feed the souls of all beings in Skyrim to a Daedric Artifact of Namira known as the Dark Heart, and use the power of the Dark Heart to sever themselves from Molag Bal - and to make themselves an army of truly immortal conquerors. [pagebreak] But to see Skyrim now, a few years into the Fourth Era? No traces remain of those storms. None remembers the terror of the Harrowstorms tearing across the settlements of the Reach. The Nords of Skyrim are as strong and boisterous as ever. Does this not demonstrate the resiliency of civilization? The land and its people remain, and none but a few dedicated historians even recall the existence of the Gray Host or their terrible storms. I believe the scars of the Oblivion Crisis will fade in much the same way. I predict that by the third century of the Fourth Era, Tamriel will barely remember this crisis. The Empire will remain strong, the people of Tamriel will remain unified, and the schemes of the daedra will be but a memory.
String.Dest:
[pagebreak]

An Argument for a Broader View of Matters by Brother Betrelion

[pagebreak] Terms such as "aedra" and "daedra" have been in common parlance for so long that we rarely remember their true meaning. At their core, these terms are quite simple: "aedra" means "our ancestors," while the modified "daedra" merely means "not our ancestors." In other words, the aedra are any spirits who sacrificed themselves to create our world, while the daedra are those who did not participate. But who today uses the terms in that manner? Think, for example, of Trinimac. None can argue his contribution to creating Nirn, and yet his transformation into Malacath renders him no longer our ancestor? Would the orcs, children of Malacath, agree with this assessment? Or perhaps we should consider Meridia. A daedra now, but formerly a child of Magnus who called herself Merid-Nunda. Indeed, some faiths still know her as such. Does she change between being an ancestor of mortals depending on who worships her? [pagebreak] Indeed, the children of Magnus - the Magna-Ge - pose their own dilemma. They certainly took part in the initial creation of Nirn, but fled before the task was done, leaving only their stars behind. Are they still Aedric? Do we now define Aedric simply as "is located in Aetherius" and disqualify those Divines who exist on Nirn? And this question assumes, of course, that Magnus has not created more children since then - an assumption we have no basis for. Let us broaden matters further. If a "good" spirit - as "aedra" is often incorrectly used to mean in modern times - is an ancestor spirit, Talos and ALMSIVI must be daedra, for they did not attain divinity until after the world already existed. And then we have the spirits of the Void to consider - beings who by definition cannot fit into any Aurbic terms due to not being native to the Aurbis, yet who are often grouped with daedra. [pagebreak] Sithis, certainly, is a being of the Void. But so was Namira, and she is unquestionably a Daedric Prince by her own admission. But what of Anu and Padomay? If one takes the Anuad as more than mere metaphor - a difficult task, admittedly - they too were born in the Void. Even the Void spirits who occasionally enter the Aurbis today, such as Millamaste and Xibbenxaml, are as different from one another as they are from mortals. Can we include them all in the same category simply due to not being members of any other category? I believe our fundamental picture of matters is flawed exactly because of this insistence on categorization. Perhaps, rather than grouping into categories such as "aedra," "daedra," "Magna-Ge," "Star-Orphan," "Void Spirit," "Divine," or any of the countless other terms one may invent, we should view them more as the Reachfolk do - simply as "spirits," regardless of further detail. Or perhaps we could take the Argonian view of these matters, which is best summed up as "who cares?" (Though, perhaps the tribesman I interviewed was simply impatient for me to leave). I am confident that those of you who read this dissertation will understand my points and will agree that, as our fundamental categorization of these matters is flawed at the core, it should not be used as a basis of judgment. You will, therefore, doubtless agree that I have committed no wrong through my extramarital liaison with a Pumpkin Spectre, and should have my membership in the priory restored.
String.Dest:
[pagebreak]

Studies of the Void: Tellijih, Vol I

[pagebreak] Ever since I learned of the existence of the Void Spirits, daedra-like beings that emerged from beyond the borders of the Aurbis, the entity known as Tellijih the Silent has been a particular interest of mine. Void worshippers are rare in general (most cultists find it more useful to beseech more "real" entities, such as the Daedric Princes, as those are far more likely to respond), but even among Void cults, worship of Tellijih is rare due to her aloof nature. Indeed, the majority of writings I found discussing her date back to the time of the Ayleids. [pagebreak] In general, the Ayleids had few issues with worship of daedra, Void entities, or any other sort of being. Their primary cults generally focused on worship of the Magna-Ge or select Princes such as Molag Bal or Merid-Nunda, but worship of Void entities such as Varanix and Gryhax Bahn was known to occur as well. The exception was a trio of Void entities they fearfully called the "Corruptors of the Stars" - Likirani the Radiant, Sondra Drel the Lugubrious, and Tellijih the Silent. Ayleids who were known to worship these three, such as those in the city of Varladimath, were shunned at best and slaughtered at worst. [pagebreak] After much effort, I managed to obtain an invitation to a meeting of modern-day Tellijih worshippers. Unlike most Void cults, these cultists were quite cordial - they could easily have been mistaken for a group of scholars meeting for tea. They explained that they worshipped Tellijih primarily as a meditative exercise, contemplating stillness and silence, with no expectation of anything in return. Surprisingly, they then invited me to meet with Tellijih personally!
String.Dest:
[pagebreak]

Surprisingly, they then invited me to meet with Tellijih personally!

String.Source:
[pagebreak]

Studies of the Void: Tellijih, Vol II

[pagebreak] While I was obviously wary that the invitation would result in my becoming a ritual sacrifice, my curiosity overpowered my concerns. The details of the ritual have left my mind, but I recall a feeling of great stillness and cold. Then there was darkness, and I felt as though I was floating. When I opened my eyes, I found myself within an enormous crystal hourglass. Instead of sand, crystals of ice floated around me, sticking to the inner surface of the glass. And before me, I beheld Tellijih herself. [pagebreak] There was a strange beauty in the avatar that the Silent Maiden had selected. In profile, she resembled a human or elvish woman, garbed in flowing brown robes and a tan cloche hat. A single golden eye gazed at me through a crystal monocle, her other eye - if one existed - concealed behind her flowing amber hair. I do not mean flowing as the metaphor it is often used as - I mean that her hair literally flowed forth, seemingly made entirely of amber liquid. The rest of her body was even more alien, for it was made entirely of gears. Not a single aspect of her was organic - every piece of her form was composed of tiny bits of clockwork, constantly ticking in a strange melody. [pagebreak] I made to speak, but found I could not move. The gaze of that golden eye seemed to entirely freeze reality - I could not help but feel that Akatosh himself would freeze if he were to meet the gaze of Tellijih. Then she lifted her eye, and the world returned. The image before me faded, and I was once more in the cult's manor. The cult leader seemed amused by my experience and assured me that I had not offended Tellijih. In all the centuries the cult had operated, none had attracted more than a single instant of the Silent Maiden's gaze. He believed that Tellijih was waiting for someone specific to serve her ends and was content to wait as many eons as it may take for that person to arrive. [pagebreak] Despite my fears, nothing further occurred during my meeting with the cultists, save for my requesting the cult leader's tea recipe. The leader offered to accept me into the group, and I confess I am still considering the offer. Tellijih's golden eye still floats in my vision whenever sleep begins to overtake me, and I find myself strangely drawn to it. But for now, I shall publish this accounting of my encounter with the Silent Maiden, in the hopes that it may be of value to others.
String.Dest:
[pagebreak]

When I opened my eyes, I found myself within an enormous crystal hourglass. Instead of sand, crystals of ice floated around me, sticking to the inner surface of the glass. And before me, I beheld Tellijih herself. [pagebreak] There was a strange beauty in the avatar that the Silent Maiden had selected. In profile, she resembled a human or elvish woman, garbed in flowing brown robes and a tan cloche hat. A single golden eye gazed at me through a crystal monocle, her other eye - if one existed - concealed behind her flowing amber hair. I do not mean flowing as the metaphor it is often used as - I mean that her hair literally flowed forth, seemingly made entirely of amber liquid. The rest of her body was even more alien, for it was made entirely of gears. Not a single aspect of her was organic - every piece of her form was composed of tiny bits of clockwork, constantly ticking in a strange melody. [pagebreak] I made to speak, but found I could not move. The gaze of that golden eye seemed to entirely freeze reality - I could not help but feel that Akatosh himself would freeze if he were to meet the gaze of Tellijih. Then she lifted her eye, and the world returned. The image before me faded, and I was once more in the cult's manor. The cult leader seemed amused by my experience and assured me that I had not offended Tellijih. In all the centuries the cult had operated, none had attracted more than a single instant of the Silent Maiden's gaze. He believed that Tellijih was waiting for someone specific to serve her ends and was content to wait as many eons as it may take for that person to arrive. [pagebreak] Despite my fears, nothing further occurred during my meeting with the cultists, save for my requesting the cult leader's tea recipe. The leader offered to accept me into the group, and I confess I am still considering the offer. Tellijih's golden eye still floats in my vision whenever sleep begins to overtake me, and I find myself strangely drawn to it. But for now, I shall publish this accounting of my encounter with the Silent Maiden, in the hopes that it may be of value to others.

String.Source:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont'><font size='18'> The key points of the tablet regarding entering the "Hollowing Chamber" are as follows, though do note that my translation is a bit imprecise.
"Seek the chamber where knowledge lines the walls, that the dark mysteries may fill thy empty mind." - A library, I presume?
"Offer thy hands to that which lacks a soul." - I assume this means placing your hands on something or perhaps pressing it. A switch of some sort, most likely. The note that you must do it to the "one which lacks a soul" appears to be a hint as to which should be pressed, so I suspect there will be some sort of rudimentary trap for those who press the wrong switch.
"Step through the false wall, and offer thy soul to the Void." - A hidden door, I presume. Whatever ritual device may await on the other side, I would advise you to avoid offering your soul to it. </font>

[pagebreak]

Worship within the Reach - My Time Among the Clans A collection of observations by Una Futtlesen. 8th of the Second Seed 4E 98

[pagebreak] Throughout my travels among the denizens of the Reach, I have learned that they are a people steeped in tradition, history through the spoken word, and deep devotion to the natural world and its wonders. Each clan varies in its rituals and rites, where no two are quite alike. Some will revere great beasts, others will offer gifts to spirits who dwell in caves or waterfalls. Others might even pray to their ancestors for guidance, victory, or even love. However, there are some spirits that each clan will worship regardless of their particular brand of faith, with one such spirit being the Prince of the Hunt - the Daedric Prince, Hircine. The Reachfolk believe that there are five main aspects to the Master of Beasts: Alrabeg the Hunter, Gulibeg the Quick Fox, Hrokkibeg the Mighty Bear, Storihbeg the Skinchanger, and Uricanbeg the Great Stag. Some revere even more facets, such as the aspect of the Owl or the Great Dark Ram, which are rumored to have been spotted in locations such as the Ilessan Hills or the Great Forest of Cyrodiil. Unlike the "lofty scholars in their temples to the Divine", the Reachmen believe that Hiricine's physical manifestations of these aspects are far more important and offer tangible lessons to heed and grow from. [pagebreak] It is said that Hircine gifted the Reach to its inhabitants as a perfect proving ground to learn from his teachings. With swathes of enemies on all sides, they can fully live in the fiercely dangerous "now" where the ever-present urgency of survival teaches the Reachfolk how to hunt, fight, and ultimately survive where others are not dedicated enough to do so. There is no rest in this kind of survival, and that constant looming threat stokes the passion in the hearts of his followers within the Reach. As I sit here, listening to tales of the majestic Hircine - Hunt-Father, Old Elk Eye, and my personal favorite, Spear with Five Points - it is a tiring endeavour to keep up with the zeal they show. I am exhausted. They are not. "There is always another hunt," is the rhetoric bandied about the camps. That sentiment always remains constant, even in death, when they are promised entry within the Hunting Grounds where the forests are teeming with great beasts, comfortable lodges are stocked with ale, warm beds, and honed weapons, and those lucky enough to prowl that plane are privy to the most spectacular hunts. [pagebreak] 2nd of Hearthfire 4E 98 The clan I am staying with currently is known as the Boldclaw Clan, and I have been roped into preparing the large bonfire that they are building in the centre of camp, where I'm told we will be engaging in a dance. Which my two left feet are very excited for. Despite my failings in graceful movement, I'm rather excited to witness what is known as "Namira's Dance". According to the stories that have been shared with me, the Reachfolk don't hold the same fear or suspicion that usual faithful folk have of the Deadric Prince, Namira. The Lady of Decay holds dominion over hunger, death, revulsion, and, you guessed it, decay. But in the heart of the Reach, her spheres of influence are not just creepy crawlies and the endless dark. Instead, they see her as both sides of the septim of life and death. They say she is an avatar of these opposing, dualistic concepts, which, as they explain them, seem less and less conflicting. [pagebreak] I can see why the Reachfolk take comfort in her, in their own morbid way. Namira, in essence, gives life and takes it, without bias in the same way a wild animal will kill its prey, or a falling tree crushes a woodsman. Yet she supports the wellspring of life too, as an avatar of rebirth. The clan witch tells me this cycle repeats until the soul finds the oldest and deepest wisdom, before ascending to become a "Voidmother." I shudder to think what a Voidmother would birth. The kind vateshran who I've been shadowing has garbed me in dark robes and face paint to symbolize death, while the others seem to be stripping nude and smearing what I really hope isn't blood over themselves... By the Eight, I hope it isn't blood.
String.Dest:
[pagebreak]

String.Source: [pagebreak] The Void Egg: A Traditional Myth of the Old Lands [pagebreak] "Tell me," the scholar said as he sipped his wine, "of the Void." The Hollow Princess, seated across from him, nodded. She selected an uncooked egg from the breakfast platter, rolling it between her long fingers. "Fertilized," she said, grinning. "You can tell from the weight." She held the egg up to the light. "Think of the Aurbis like this egg." The scholar nodded and took another sip of wine. "Aetherius is the shell. It wraps all of reality within itself. Below that is the white - that is, Oblivion. A swirling mass of potential, but nothing truly formed. If one seeks form, they require the physical plane - Mundus." "Mundus is the chick, then?" The scholar asked. The Princess shook her head. "The yolk is not what forms the chick. It nurtures and feeds the chick as it grows, but the chick is separate. Much like how mortal souls will one day grow beyond the Aurbis." "AMARANTH," the scholar said, nodding. He hoped this made him seem intelligent, though he was not entirely sure of the meaning of what he had just said. "Perhaps. Perhaps not." The Princess examined the egg, uninterested in the scholar's words. "Regardless, you may consider that the Aurbis. Aetherius and Oblivion surround the Mundus, a realm meant to nurture mortal souls." She grinned again. The scholar noticed how very sharp her teeth were. "If reality is all within this egg, then the Void is everything outside of it." The scholar took another sip of wine. "But why worship the Void, then? If it is outside of everything-" The Princess clenched her fist, crushing the egg and the unborn chick within. "A foolish question." She let out a slow chuckle. "Does not every chick dream of breaking free from the egg?" The scholar could not answer, for the poison within the wine had done its purpose.

String.Dest: In the depths of the ruins, we encountered a strange rift in the world. I should investigate.

String.Source: When Audrey approached the rift, it suddenly vanished. I should ask her what happened.
String.Dest: When Audrey approached the rift, it suddenly vanished. I should ask her what happened.

String.Source: It seems Audrey absorbed the Void energy from the rift, sealing it away and increasing her strength. I should ask her if she remembers any other places where these rifts may have formed.
String.Dest: It seems Audrey absorbed the Void energy from the rift, sealing it away and increasing her strength. I should ask her if she remembers any other places where these rifts may have formed.

String.Source: With the four smaller wards destroyed, the final ward in the central chamber should be exposed.
String.Dest: With the four smaller wards destroyed, the final ward in the central chamber should be exposed.

String.Dest: Destroying the last of the wards seems to have summoned a guardian. I'll need to destroy it to proceed.

String.Source: The wards have been destroyed. I should tell the Lector the good news.
String.Dest: The wards have been destroyed. I should tell the Lector the good news.

String.Source: The wards have been destroyed. Hopefully this will lessen the torment of the Icebloods trapped in the ruins.
String.Dest: The wards have been destroyed. Hopefully this will lessen the torment of the Icebloods trapped in the ruins.

String.Dest: Audrey mentioned remembering a strange dark cave in a place filled with Forsworn symbols and ruins. There may be another breach there - we should investigate.

String.Source: Audrey's memories seemed to be of the ruins of the Dark Descent below Lost Valley Redoubt. I should explore and see if we can find another breach left over from Rukar's experiments.
String.Dest: Audrey's memories seemed to be of the ruins of the Dark Descent below Lost Valley Redoubt. I should explore and see if we can find another breach left over from Rukar's experiments.

String.Source: Like before, we found a breach in reality below the Dark Descent. Hopefully, Audrey's presence will be enough to dispel it.
String.Dest: Like before, we found a breach in reality below the Dark Descent. Hopefully, Audrey's presence will be enough to dispel it.

String.Dest: Audrey seems to have dispelled the breach. I should check on her.

String.Dest: Once again, Audrey has absorbed the magic from the breach, sealing it in the process.

String.Source: An alien voice greeted me upon entering the cave. A strange sense of dread hangs over everything, like something terrible has been unleashed.
String.Dest: An alien voice greeted me upon entering the cave. A strange sense of dread hangs over everything, like something terrible has been unleashed.

String.Source: The voice introduced itself as Kalarix Brood, the Writhing Mother - an entity from the Void that has allied itself with Namira. Kalarix demanded I contaminate the meals of Skyrim's jarls with parasite eggs to spread her influence. Unless I obey her - or find some way to destroy the eggs - I will become her next victim.
String.Dest: The voice introduced itself as Kalarix Brood, the Writhing Mother - an entity from the Void that has allied itself with Namira. Kalarix demanded I contaminate the meals of Skyrim's jarls with parasite eggs to spread her influence. Unless I obey her - or find some way to destroy the eggs - I will become her next victim.

String.Source: As Kalarix Brood commanded, I have contaminated the meals of Skyrim's leaders with parasite eggs. She has now instructed me to return to her shrine for my reward.
String.Dest: As Kalarix Brood commanded, I have contaminated the meals of Skyrim's leaders with parasite eggs. She has now instructed me to return to her shrine for my reward.

String.Source: As Kalarix Brood commanded, I have contaminated the meals of Skyrim's leaders with parasite eggs. She now commands me to approach her shrine.
String.Dest: As Kalarix Brood commanded, I have contaminated the meals of Skyrim's leaders with parasite eggs. She now commands me to approach her shrine.

String.Source: Kalarix Brood was pleased with my efforts on her behalf. My award waits on a pedestal below her shrine.
String.Dest: Kalarix Brood was pleased with my efforts on her behalf. My award waits on a pedestal below her shrine.

String.Source: Kalarix Brood was pleased with my efforts on her behalf and awarded me the use of Blood-Burrower, an artifact of the Writhing Brood. Before granting me the weapon, Kalarix informed me that she will be watching my future exploits - as will her fellow Void entities.
String.Dest: Kalarix Brood was pleased with my efforts on her behalf and awarded me the use of Blood-Burrower, an artifact of the Writhing Brood. Before granting me the weapon, Kalarix informed me that she will be watching my future exploits - as will her fellow Void entities.

String.Source: I have destroyed the cursed parasite eggs, sparing Skyrim from further infiltration by servants of the Writhing Brood - at least for now. Despite her obvious anger, Kalarix chose not to punish me, though it would still be wise to ensure all my meals are well-cooked for a while.
String.Dest: I have destroyed the cursed parasite eggs, sparing Skyrim from further infiltration by servants of the Writhing Brood - at least for now. Despite her obvious anger, Kalarix chose not to punish me, though it would still be wise to ensure all my meals are well-cooked for a while.

String.Source: I awoke in an unfamiliar house. The villager here seems to have rescued me from the cave-in. He said some strange things about "Meat" and "Blood," but he left before I could ask him anything. For now, I suppose I should check that "Meat" he offered me.
String.Dest: I awoke in an unfamiliar house. The villager here seems to have rescued me from the cave-in. He said some strange things about "Meat" and "Blood," but he left before I could ask him anything. For now, I suppose I should check that "Meat" he offered me.

String.Dest: Something appeared behind me as soon as I approached the Meat. It resembles a doll, but it spoke... What kind of entity is it?

String.Source: The doll introduced itself - herself? - as Audrey. She doesn't seem like an enemy, but as for what she is... Any chance for further questions was interrupted by the sound of the villager's screams. I should hurry to the basement and investigate.
String.Dest: The doll introduced itself - herself? - as Audrey. She doesn't seem like an enemy, but as for what she is... Any chance for further questions was interrupted by the sound of the villager's screams. I should hurry to the basement and investigate.

String.Dest: The villager who helped me is dead at the hands of a trio of crazed attackers with bleeding eyes. Whatever is going on, I need to defend myself.

String.Source: The attackers are dead. I need some answers about what's going on.
String.Dest: The attackers are dead. I need some answers about what's going on.

String.Source: Audrey was evasive when asked for details. I'll need to see this village myself if I want answers.
String.Dest: Audrey was evasive when asked for details. I'll need to see this village myself if I want answers.

String.Source: I ran into an elderly hunter as I exited the villager's basement. Perhaps he can explain more.
String.Dest: I ran into an elderly hunter as I exited the villager's basement. Perhaps he can explain more.

String.Dest: Rukar promised to explain more, as long as I can spare some time for him.

String.Source: Rukar wanted to speak with me. I should ask what he needs.
String.Dest: Rukar wanted to speak with me. I should ask what he needs.

String.Source: Rukar is explaining the situation to me. I should pay attention.
String.Dest: Rukar is explaining the situation to me. I should pay attention.

String.Source: Rukar explained the gist of the situation. The villagers in this realm - the Old Lands - rely on something known as the "Old Blood," which they believe is the blood of the god Lorkhan and which flows from roots throughout this realm. Within the last few decades, the Old Blood has begun to dry up, and the villagers are beginning to succumb to madness. Rukar says he has a plan, but needs my help to accomplish it.
String.Dest: Rukar explained the gist of the situation. The villagers in this realm - the Old Lands - rely on something known as the "Old Blood," which they believe is the blood of the god Lorkhan and which flows from roots throughout this realm. Within the last few decades, the Old Blood has begun to dry up, and the villagers are beginning to succumb to madness. Rukar says he has a plan, but needs my help to accomplish it.

String.Source: To find the source of the Blood, Rukar says I'll need to ring five bells throughout the Old Lands. The first three are located in the desert ruins, the haunted forest, and in the church overlooking Dry Sands Village.
String.Dest: To find the source of the Blood, Rukar says I'll need to ring five bells throughout the Old Lands. The first three are located in the desert ruins, the haunted forest, and in the church overlooking Dry Sands Village.

String.Dest: All three bells have been rung. I should return to Rukar and see if the villager's bell has been repaired.

String.Source: The bell is repaired. It's time to ring it - hopefully the legend about the four bells "pointing the way to the fifth" will prove true.
String.Dest: The bell is repaired. It's time to ring it - hopefully the legend about the four bells "pointing the way to the fifth" will prove true.

String.Dest: When I rang the fourth bell, a sudden quake occurred, revealing a cave. Could that be where the final bell is hidden?

String.Source: One of the bells I need to ring is located in the desert ruins.
String.Dest: One of the bells I need to ring is located in the desert ruins.

String.Dest: The belltower is locked. I'll need to find the key to get inside.

String.Dest: I've found the key to enter the belltower.

String.Source: The belltower is guarded by a pair of Rajaska. I'll need to slay them to proceed.
String.Dest: The belltower is guarded by a pair of Rajaska. I'll need to slay them to proceed.

String.Dest: The Rajaska are dead. I can now ring the bell.

String.Source: I've rung the bell in the ruins.
String.Dest: I've rung the bell in the ruins.

String.Source: We've escaped the throne room and have arrived in some sort of underground tunnel.
String.Dest: We've escaped the throne room and have arrived in some sort of underground tunnel.

String.Source: We'll need to delve deeper into these tunnels if we're going to cut off the Hollow Princess from her source of power.
String.Dest: We'll need to delve deeper into these tunnels if we're going to cut off the Hollow Princess from her source of power.

String.Source: The source of the Blood is finally in sight. A massive Hist Tree, with roots stretching throughout the entirety of the Old Lands.
String.Dest: The source of the Blood is finally in sight. A massive Hist Tree, with roots stretching throughout the entirety of the Old Lands.

String.Source: The Hollow Princess will never die as long as the Hist Tree is sustaining her. Destroying the Hist is the only way to break the curse on the Old Lands.
String.Dest: The Hollow Princess will never die as long as the Hist Tree is sustaining her. Destroying the Hist is the only way to break the curse on the Old Lands.

String.Dest: The tree is dead, and the cavern has collapsed. I should speak with Audrey.

String.Source: Audrey has explained the truth: Rukar, the old man trusted by many of the villagers, is in fact her creator - and a dark mage seeking world domination. With the mutant Hist Tree dead, Rukar is the prime threat remaining in the Old Lands. I should return to the village and pursue him.
String.Dest: Audrey has explained the truth: Rukar, the old man trusted by many of the villagers, is in fact her creator - and a dark mage seeking world domination. With the mutant Hist Tree dead, Rukar is the prime threat remaining in the Old Lands. I should return to the village and pursue him.

String.Dest: Rukar left behind some magical defenses in his house, but I've found a lead - a note indicating a hidden lair deep in the forest, by a circle of standing stones. The note mentions using a Voidlight spell to expose the lair. I can either cast it myself or ask Audrey to cast it for me.

String.Dest: Audrey remembered another fragment of Rukar's journey to create her. A Dwarven ruin, mostly collapsed, near a source of Aetherium ore. Near Deep Folk Crossing, possibly?

String.Dest: One of the bells I need to ring is located in the Church of the Old Blood. Hopefully the priestess will be reasonable.

String.Dest: Zenkali-Dra, Priestess of the Old Blood, refused to grant me access to the sealed belltower. If I want to ring the bell, I will need to earn her trust by increasing the supply of Meat from the mines.

String.Dest: Overseer Dokazeek says they cannot produce more Meat as long as the monsters continue to infest the Mines. He's given me a key to the Mines and tasked me with finding where the monsters are coming from.

String.Dest: I've stumbled upon a strange portal in the depths of the Meat Mines. It seems this is the source of the monsters. I'll need to find a way to seal it.

String.Dest: The portal in the mines has been sealed. The mines are still overrun with the monsters that already came through, but hopefully no new ones will arrive. I should report to Overseer Dokazeek.

String.Source: I convinced Dokazeek to give the Church as much Meat as the miners can spare. I should tell Zenkali-Dra the good news.
String.Dest: I convinced Dokazeek to give the Church as much Meat as the miners can spare. I should tell Zenkali-Dra the good news.

String.Source: I accepted Overseer Dokazeek's deal to use his information to sneak into the Church and ring the bell that way. Dokazeek will do his best to assuage Zenkali-Dra's anger while I do that. Hopefully he succeeds.
String.Dest: I accepted Overseer Dokazeek's deal to use his information to sneak into the Church and ring the bell that way. Dokazeek will do his best to assuage Zenkali-Dra's anger while I do that. Hopefully he succeeds.

String.Source: Zenkali-Dra was waiting to ambush me when I arrived in the church.
String.Dest: Zenkali-Dra was waiting to ambush me when I arrived in the church.

String.Source: It took a while, but I've finally gained the key to the belfry. It's time to get this over with.
String.Dest: It took a while, but I've finally gained the key to the belfry. It's time to get this over with.

String.Source: I've reached the belfry. Time to ring the bell.
String.Dest: I've reached the belfry. Time to ring the bell.

String.Source: I've rung the bell in the Church of the Old Blood.
String.Dest: I've rung the bell in the Church of the Old Blood.

String.Source: Ringing the fourth bell revealed a hidden tunnel near the center of the village. Could the final bell be within?
String.Dest: Ringing the fourth bell revealed a hidden tunnel near the center of the village. Could the final bell be within?

String.Source: I've entered the tunnel. Time to find out where it leads.
String.Dest: I've entered the tunnel. Time to find out where it leads.

String.Source: I've found myself in a strange frozen area filled with massive ruins. I should investigate further.
String.Dest: I've found myself in a strange frozen area filled with massive ruins. I should investigate further.

String.Source: A living Snow Elf greeted me upon entering the ruins. I should ask him for more information.
String.Dest: A living Snow Elf greeted me upon entering the ruins. I should ask him for more information.

String.Source: Lector Mirthraeyl says the bell is on the far side of the ruins, but I'll need to take the long way through the ruins to get there.
String.Dest: Lector Mirthraeyl says the bell is on the far side of the ruins, but I'll need to take the long way through the ruins to get there.

String.Source: I've reached the other side of the ruins. The belltower should be ahead.
String.Dest: I've reached the other side of the ruins. The belltower should be ahead.

String.Source: The belltower is guarded by an ancient Atronach. I'll need to defeat it to proceed.
String.Dest: The belltower is guarded by an ancient Atronach. I'll need to defeat it to proceed.

String.Source: I've defeated the Atronach and can now reach the bell.
String.Dest: I've defeated the Atronach and can now reach the bell.

String.Source: I've reached the final bell. Time to ring it.
String.Dest: I've reached the final bell. Time to ring it.

String.Source: The final bell has been rung.
String.Dest: The final bell has been rung.

String.Source: The bells have all been rung. The barrier blocking entry into the Hollow Palace should finally be open.
String.Dest: The bells have all been rung. The barrier blocking entry into the Hollow Palace should finally be open.

String.Source: We've entered the Hollow Palace. The source of the Blood is likely through the throne room.
String.Dest: We've entered the Hollow Palace. The source of the Blood is likely through the throne room.

String.Source: The throne room is blocked by a magic barrier. There are two switches by the barrier, but they are locked. Another trial by the Princess?
String.Dest: The throne room is blocked by a magic barrier. There are two switches by the barrier, but they are locked. Another trial by the Princess?

String.Source: I've gotten both keys and can now lower the barrier and enter the throne room.
String.Dest: I've gotten both keys and can now lower the barrier and enter the throne room.

String.Source: The Hollow Princess lives - or, at least, her spirit does, in the form of a powerful Voidmother. I'll need to defeat her.
String.Dest: The Hollow Princess lives - or, at least, her spirit does, in the form of a powerful Voidmother. I'll need to defeat her.

String.Source: Nothing I do seems capable of inflicting lasting harm to the Princess. I have no choice but to flee. One of her attacks revealed a tunnel behind a wall - that may be my only hope.
String.Dest: Nothing I do seems capable of inflicting lasting harm to the Princess. I have no choice but to flee. One of her attacks revealed a tunnel behind a wall - that may be my only hope.

String.Source: Nothing I do seems capable of inflicting lasting harm to the Princess. I had no choice but to flee into the tunnels beyond the throne room.
String.Dest: Nothing I do seems capable of inflicting lasting harm to the Princess. I had no choice but to flee into the tunnels beyond the throne room.

String.Source: Can create armor and weapons at forges using the Old Blood, and improve them twice as much.
String.Dest: Can create armor and weapons at forges using the Old Blood, and improve them twice as much.

String.Source: Vessel is 100% harder to detect.
String.Dest: Vessel is 100% harder to detect.

String.Source: Audrey becomes <1>% stronger for every void gem given, up to a maximum of <100>%.
String.Dest: Audrey becomes <1>% stronger for every void gem given, up to a maximum of <100>%.

String.Source: Health is increased by 50 points.
String.Dest: Health is increased by 50 points.

String.Source: Health is increased by 40 points.
String.Dest: Health is increased by 40 points.

String.Source: Health is increased by 30 points.
String.Dest: Health is increased by 30 points.

String.Source: Health is increased by 20 points.
String.Dest: Health is increased by 20 points.

String.Source: Health is increased by 10 points.
String.Dest: Health is increased by 10 points.

String.Source: Make Audrey go easy on enemies.
String.Dest: Make Audrey go easy on enemies.

String.Source: Reduces armor on hit.
String.Dest: Reduces armor on hit.

String.Source: Making shades suck that little bit more.
String.Dest: Making shades suck that little bit more.

String.Source: While difficult to fully translate, this tablet appears to include a warning not to pet the voriplasms.
String.Dest: While difficult to fully translate, this tablet appears to include a warning not to pet the voriplasms.

String.Source: The Aspect's death strips the Moon Beast of power.
String.Dest: The Aspect's death strips the Moon Beast of power.

String.Source: Potions removed from Thorntaker's satchel.
String.Dest: Potions removed from Thorntaker's satchel.

String.Source: Ancheta's request requires Duraeg's Effects.
String.Dest: Ancheta's request requires Duraeg's Effects.

String.Source: Mehela Crow-Watcher's request requires one Sload Soap.
String.Dest: Mehela Crow-Watcher's request requires one Sload Soap.

String.Source: Those who refuse to serve Namiira in life may still serve in death. Here their bodies are sacrificed, that their souls may be shaped by the grasp of darkness. May all who perish find themselves shackled to her service! UR DRA NA MII RA! UR DRA NA MII RA!
String.Dest: Those who refuse to serve Namiira in life may still serve in death. Here their bodies are sacrificed, that their souls may be shaped by the grasp of darkness. May all who perish find themselves shackled to her service! UR DRA NA MII RA! UR DRA NA MII RA!

String.Source: Falls-Off-Ledges' request requires one Red Book of Riddles.
String.Dest: Falls-Off-Ledges' request requires one Red Book of Riddles.

String.Source: Digs-the-Depths' request requires three Voriplasmic Bloodroots.
String.Dest: Digs-the-Depths' request requires three Voriplasmic Bloodroots.

String.Source: Hears-the-Roots' request requires ten lumps of Clay.
String.Dest: Hears-the-Roots' request requires ten lumps of Clay.

String.Source: This appears to connect to the neighboring xanmeer of Reezal-Bak.
String.Dest: This appears to connect to the neighboring xanmeer of Reezal-Bak.

String.Source: This message is difficult to decipher, but it seems to refer to "Daughters of Sithis."
String.Dest: This message is difficult to decipher, but it seems to refer to "Daughters of Sithis."

String.Source: This appears to be intended to hold some sort of staff, but whatever is in it was removed. Judging by the lack of dust, whatever was taken from here was taken recently.
String.Dest: This appears to be intended to hold some sort of staff, but whatever is in it was removed. Judging by the lack of dust, whatever was taken from here was taken recently.

String.Source: Audrey cannot yet leave the Old Lands. She will gain this ability as you progress further in the search for the source of the Blood. Until then, she will rejoin you when you return to the Old Lands.
String.Dest: Audrey cannot yet leave the Old Lands. She will gain this ability as you progress further in the search for the source of the Blood. Until then, she will rejoin you when you return to the Old Lands.

String.Source: You have an outdated version of A Tale of Blood and Snow installed. Heart of the Mountain's integration features will not work properly. Please update to A Tale of Blood and Snow version 2.35 or newer. This message will only be displayed once.
String.Dest: You have an outdated version of A Tale of Blood and Snow installed. Heart of the Mountain's integration features will not work properly. Please update to A Tale of Blood and Snow version 2.35 or newer. This message will only be displayed once.

String.Source: Of those who offered their blood to the Princess, one was a coward. They offered the blood of another in their stead, and so her servant struck them down with the thief's pick.
String.Dest: Of those who offered their blood to the Princess, one was a coward. They offered the blood of another in their stead, and so her servant struck them down with the thief's pick.

String.Source: Whatever this is, it doesn't seem to respond to you... Perhaps it requires someone more closely attuned to it.
String.Dest: Whatever this is, it doesn't seem to respond to you... Perhaps it requires someone more closely attuned to it.

String.Source: The survivors begged the Princess for mercy, for their Blood had run dry. And so the Princess took a single goblet of Blood, and offered it to one of those present. All others were abandoned. But to whom did she grant this blessing?
String.Dest: The survivors begged the Princess for mercy, for their Blood had run dry. And so the Princess took a single goblet of Blood, and offered it to one of those present. All others were abandoned. But to whom did she grant this blessing?

String.Source: You have no Blood to offer.
String.Dest: You have no Blood to offer.

String.Source: Any power this shrine once had has long since faded.
String.Dest: Any power this shrine once had has long since faded.

String.Source: "Show me mercy, and I shall spread the word of your glory across the world!" Is this groveling supplicant worthy of the Blood?
String.Dest: "Show me mercy, and I shall spread the word of your glory across the world!" Is this groveling supplicant worthy of the Blood?

String.Source:
"Please, I beg of you! The blood I gave you was the last of my own - I can feel my veins drying for lack of Blood!"
Give the Blood to the Dryblood supplicant?
String.Dest:
"Please, I beg of you! The blood I gave you was the last of my own - I can feel my veins drying for lack of Blood!"
Give the Blood to the Dryblood supplicant?

String.Source:
This root was injured by the thief's pick. It will likely wither soon.
Give Blood to the injured Bloodroot?
String.Dest:
This root was injured by the thief's pick. It will likely wither soon.
Give Blood to the injured Bloodroot?

String.Source:
"I am already doomed for daring to think of defying you. Please, all I ask is a final share of Blood, that I may die as myself!"
Give Blood to the despondent supplicant?
String.Dest:
"I am already doomed for daring to think of defying you. Please, all I ask is a final share of Blood, that I may die as myself!"
Give Blood to the despondent supplicant?

String.Source:
Perhaps none are worthy. The soil has more value than their lives.
Pour the Blood into the sand?
String.Dest:
Perhaps none are worthy. The soil has more value than their lives.
Pour the Blood into the sand?

String.Source: You cannot fast travel at present.
String.Dest: You cannot fast travel at present.

String.Source: A man once sought to defy the Princess. He thought to steal the Blood. He took his pick of bone and swung it at the largest root he found, thinking he would tunnel back to the source.
String.Dest: A man once sought to defy the Princess. He thought to steal the Blood. He took his pick of bone and swung it at the largest root he found, thinking he would tunnel back to the source.

String.Source: It seems this was not correct. Guessing randomly may have consequences...
String.Dest: It seems this was not correct. Guessing randomly may have consequences...

String.Source: It seems this will only respond when struck with a specific weapon.
String.Dest: It seems this will only respond when struck with a specific weapon.

String.Source: Audrey approves.
String.Dest: Audrey approves.

String.Source: Audrey disapproves.
String.Dest: Audrey disapproves.

String.Source: Nirigirath Thysus, Founder of the Iceblood Clan
String.Dest: Nirigirath Thysus, Founder of the Iceblood Clan

String.Source: Lector Lilyandyis, First among the Scholars
String.Dest: Lector Lilyandyis, First among the Scholars

String.Source: Lector Mirthraeyl, Keeper of the Academy
String.Dest: Lector Mirthraeyl, Keeper of the Academy

String.Source: Lector Sindronal, who learned of the Star
String.Dest: Lector Sindronal, who learned of the Star

String.Source: Vyragoth Emnal, who sacrificed himself to fend off the Atmorans
String.Dest: Vyragoth Emnal, who sacrificed himself to fend off the Atmorans

String.Dest: Whatever was written here has long since been worn away

String.Source: This message appears to be a warning of some sort, but the years have eroded anything intelligible.
String.Dest: This message appears to be a warning of some sort, but the years have eroded anything intelligible.

String.Source: These tools are still pumping something into the roots. Smashing them would put a stop to that.

String.Source: Here we imprison the winds of Khenarthi, that they may never again carry the cats to prosperity. Let the dry sands drain their souls! May the will of our Rajaska drive the cats to their doom! UR DRA NA MII RA! UR DRA NA MII RA!
String.Dest: Here we imprison the winds of Khenarthi, that they may never again carry the cats to prosperity. Let the dry sands drain their souls! May the will of our Rajaska drive the cats to their doom! UR DRA NA MII RA! UR DRA NA MII RA!

String.Source: If the cats will not dance, neither will they dream. Here we imprison the souls of the dreaming cats, that their sleep will be filled with Varmiina's nightmares, to torment them until they submit. May all cats fall to the Darkness! UR DRA NA MII RA! UR DRA NA MII RA!
String.Dest: If the cats will not dance, neither will they dream. Here we imprison the souls of the dreaming cats, that their sleep will be filled with Varmiina's nightmares, to torment them until they submit. May all cats fall to the Darkness! UR DRA NA MII RA! UR DRA NA MII RA!

String.Dest: Blood Sculptor Added

String.Source: Vix cannot be summoned here.
String.Dest: Vix cannot be summoned here.

String.Dest: Audrey cannot be summoned here.

String.Source: "The Hollow Princess" added to the Singing Stone in Rootwatch.
String.Dest: "The Hollow Princess" added to the Singing Stone in Rootwatch.

String.Source: Audrey cannot follow you here. She will rejoin you once you return to a place she can enter.
String.Dest: Audrey cannot follow you here. She will rejoin you once you return to a place she can enter.

String.Source: This breach can only be sealed by Audrey.
String.Dest: This breach can only be sealed by Audrey.

String.Source: Even in death, the cats will not escape the torment of Namiira. Here we seal their souls within the cursed Skull of Varmiina, to suffer eternally until they give in to despair. All shall fall to Darkness. Ur Dra Na Mii Ra! UR DRA NA MII RA!
String.Dest: Even in death, the cats will not escape the torment of Namiira. Here we seal their souls within the cursed Skull of Varmiina, to suffer eternally until they give in to despair. All shall fall to Darkness. Ur Dra Na Mii Ra! UR DRA NA MII RA!

String.Source: Audrey cannot leave the Old Lands, at least not yet. She will rejoin you once you return.
String.Dest: Audrey cannot leave the Old Lands, at least not yet. She will rejoin you once you return.

String.Source: When his pick struck the great Bloodroot the ground erupted, ensnaring him within countless roots. They pierced his flesh, drawing forth his blood as though it was water. And when those who knew the thief came upon his corpse, they knew the Princess could inflict the same punishment upon them. Offering their blood to the Princess, they embraced despair.
String.Dest: When his pick struck the great Bloodroot the ground erupted, ensnaring him within countless roots. They pierced his flesh, drawing forth his blood as though it was water. And when those who knew the thief came upon his corpse, they knew the Princess could inflict the same punishment upon them. Offering their blood to the Princess, they embraced despair.

String.Source: You lack the goblet needed to carry this.
String.Dest: You lack the goblet needed to carry this.

String.Source: While most of the details are difficult to translate, this tablet appears to contain a notice banning the play of Teeba-Hatsei within the hallways.
String.Dest: While most of the details are difficult to translate, this tablet appears to contain a notice banning the play of Teeba-Hatsei within the hallways.

String.Dest: Song "Ruins of the Saxhleel" added to the Singing Stone in Rootwatch.

String.Source: "The Thirsting Woods" added to the Singing Stone in Rootwatch.
String.Dest: "The Thirsting Woods" added to the Singing Stone in Rootwatch.

String.Source: You know, back in the Old Lands, a lot of houses doubled as shops. I'd like to try that here too, if it's okay with you.
String.Dest: You know, back in the Old Lands, a lot of houses doubled as shops. I'd like to try that here too, if it's okay with you.

String.Source: If I'm going to be living here for a while, I suppose I'll start up a shop. Might not have the same selection as back in the Old Lands, of course.
String.Dest: If I'm going to be living here for a while, I suppose I'll start up a shop. Might not have the same selection as back in the Old Lands, of course.

String.Source: It is a good home. But this one is not content to sit idle... Perhaps he will open a store.
String.Dest: It is a good home. But this one is not content to sit idle... Perhaps he will open a store.

String.Source: This is a lovely home. Perhaps I will make a shop here as well - something to keep busy while you are away.
String.Dest: This is a lovely home. Perhaps I will make a shop here as well - something to keep busy while you are away.

String.Source: Welcome back, my dear!
String.Dest: Welcome back, my dear!

String.Source: Hello, sweetie! I was going to clean the place, but... actually, I don't have an excuse.
String.Dest: Hello, sweetie! I was going to clean the place, but... actually, I don't have an excuse.

String.Source: You're back! I missed you!
String.Dest: You're back! I missed you!

String.Source: Let me know if you need anything!
String.Dest: Let me know if you need anything!

String.Source: Welcome back, my sweet.
String.Dest: Welcome back, my sweet.

String.Source: Yes, darling?
String.Dest: Yes, darling?

String.Source: Seeing you warms this one's heart.
String.Dest: Seeing you warms this one's heart.

String.Source: Welcome home. I raise my hands in welcome.
String.Dest: Welcome home. I raise my hands in welcome.

String.Source: It returns from an adventure! I am pleased to see it well.
String.Dest: It returns from an adventure! I am pleased to see it well.

String.Source: We've a wedding to get to. We can have fun after.
String.Dest: We've a wedding to get to. We can have fun after.

String.Source: We can talk later. It is time to prepare our marriage ceremony.
String.Dest: We can talk later. It is time to prepare our marriage ceremony.

String.Source: I will meet it at the Temple of Mara.
String.Dest: I will meet it at the Temple of Mara.

String.Source: Hehehe... Hehehehehehee... Heheheh... It still doesn't feel real!
String.Dest: Hehehe... Hehehehehehee... Heheheh... It still doesn't feel real!

String.Source: Me, a bride? If I could sleep, I'd think I was dreaming!
String.Dest: Me, a bride? If I could sleep, I'd think I was dreaming!

String.Source: Hehe... Heh... Ahem.
String.Dest: Hehe... Heh... Ahem.

String.Source: Well... I, uh... I guess I'm moving in with you, huh?
String.Dest: Well... I, uh... I guess I'm moving in with you, huh?

String.Source: Where is home, anyway?
String.Dest: Where is home, anyway?

String.Source: Well, that's that. I suppose we should discuss living accommodations, hm?
String.Dest: Well, that's that. I suppose we should discuss living accommodations, hm?

String.Source: I'd prefer not to return to that forest shack, if it's all the same to you.
String.Dest: I'd prefer not to return to that forest shack, if it's all the same to you.

String.Source: Married. It was not a future this one expected, but it is a good one.
String.Dest: Married. It was not a future this one expected, but it is a good one.

String.Source: Where shall we live? This one's old home would not be suitable for a family.
String.Dest: Where shall we live? This one's old home would not be suitable for a family.

String.Source: The sun shines brightly in my heart. This is a day of great joy.
String.Dest: The sun shines brightly in my heart. This is a day of great joy.

String.Source: We are bonded now. All that remains is to select where we will make our nest.
String.Dest: We are bonded now. All that remains is to select where we will make our nest.

String.Source: You are a cruel one, aren't you?! That just makes you more amusing, you know.
String.Dest: You are a cruel one, aren't you?! That just makes you more amusing, you know.

String.Source: Well, shall we return to slaying our enemies, then? I've some... frustration... to get out of my system.
String.Dest: Well, shall we return to slaying our enemies, then? I've some... frustration... to get out of my system.

String.Source: Your words are as cruel as any spat from the maw of Namiira.
String.Dest: Your words are as cruel as any spat from the maw of Namiira.

String.Source: This one wants nothing to do with you. Begone.
String.Dest: This one wants nothing to do with you. Begone.

String.Source: You are crueler than any monster. Get out!
String.Dest: You are crueler than any monster. Get out!

String.Source: Hm. I suppose so.
String.Dest: Hm. I suppose so.

String.Source: Don't lose your nerve this time, hm?
String.Dest: Don't lose your nerve this time, hm?

String.Source: Even the bravest warrior feels the chill of fear when gazing into the darkness. It is not a source of shame.
String.Dest: Even the bravest warrior feels the chill of fear when gazing into the darkness. It is not a source of shame.

String.Source: Let us redo this ceremony, without fear this time.
String.Dest: Let us redo this ceremony, without fear this time.

String.Source: It asks much of us... but very well. I will give it another chance.
String.Dest: It asks much of us... but very well. I will give it another chance.

String.Source: Whatever happened? Cold feet?
String.Dest: Whatever happened? Cold feet?

String.Source: What happened? Why did you stop the ceremony?
String.Dest: What happened? Why did you stop the ceremony?

String.Source: What is it thinking?! Why does it abandon us?
String.Dest: What is it thinking?! Why does it abandon us?

String.Source: I wasn't expecting to be so nervous... Is this really okay? I mean, I'm not even... alive, you know?
String.Dest: I wasn't expecting to be so nervous... Is this really okay? I mean, I'm not even... alive, you know?

String.Source: You... Agggh!
String.Dest: You... Agggh!

String.Source: I should have known better.
String.Dest: I should have known better.

String.Source: Just... Just leave, okay? I need time to think.
String.Dest: Just... Just leave, okay? I need time to think.

String.Source: Oh? Changed your mind after all, hm? How disappointing.
String.Dest: Oh? Changed your mind after all, hm? How disappointing.

String.Source: Leave. I need time to think.
String.Dest: Leave. I need time to think.

String.Source: All these people... All to watch us. Let's give them a good show, hm?
String.Dest: All these people... All to watch us. Let's give them a good show, hm?

String.Source: So many witnesses. You draw many friends into your pride.
String.Dest: So many witnesses. You draw many friends into your pride.

String.Source: So many guests! It has truly gathered many friends.
String.Dest: So many guests! It has truly gathered many friends.

String.Source: I'll hold down the fort until you return, my love.
String.Dest: I'll hold down the fort until you return, my love.

String.Source: Take me with you sometime. I miss adventuring with you.
String.Dest: Take me with you sometime. I miss adventuring with you.

String.Source: A real home... Hehehe, this is so exciting!
String.Dest: A real home... Hehehe, this is so exciting!

String.Source: Better than a shack in the forest, I'm sure.
String.Dest: Better than a shack in the forest, I'm sure.

String.Source: Very well. This one will meet you there.
String.Dest: Very well. This one will meet you there.

String.Source: Alright, let's head over.
String.Dest: Alright, let's head over.

String.Source: Very well. Let's be off.
String.Dest: Very well. Let's be off.

String.Source: Oh? Where will we make our new den?
String.Dest: Oh? Where will we make our new den?

String.Source: Oh? Where will we make our new nest?
String.Dest: Oh? Where will we make our new nest?

String.Source: Then I will head there at once.
String.Dest: Then I will head there at once.

String.Source: Very well. I will pack my things.
String.Dest: Very well. I will pack my things.

String.Source: Oh, really? Where to?
String.Dest: Oh, really? Where to?

String.Source: Hm? Where to?
String.Dest: Hm? Where to?

String.Source: This one likes that idea. He will pack his things and prepare to move.
String.Dest: This one likes that idea. He will pack his things and prepare to move.
